The zephyr drake is a distant cousin of the wyvern, bearing the same lean predatory frame but with sweeping feathers instead of scales. Its wings are broad and powerful, allowing it to ride ocean winds for days without landing, and its long tail ends in plumes rather than a venomous stinger. Native to the skies above the Forgotten Sea, zephyr drakes are most often sighted gliding over waves or nesting along sheer coastal cliffs. Though capable of devastating cattle herds and other livestock, they rarely attack intelligent folk, preferring easier prey.

subclassFeature.name: Path of the Provoked
entries: Though the farmers and smiths of the Tvar are often considered among the most cordial of the raiders, when pushed too hard, the Provoked Barbarian retaliates swiftly and with no measure of mercy. Some who have witnessed such unleashed carnage swear they see two warriors, standing back-to-back.

subclassFeature.name: Strength of One
entries: You score a Critical Hit on a roll of 19 or 20 on the d20 with melee attacks using a weapon or Unarmed Strike. If there are two enemies within 5 feet of you, you score a Critical Hit on rolls of 18, 19, or 20.
In addition, when you enter your Rage, you choose one of the following options. You benefit from that option until your Rage ends.

entries.name: Stoic Strength
entries: When you take damage from a creature you can see, you can use your Reaction to move up to half your Speed toward that creature. This movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks.

entries.name: Wrathful Strength
entries: When you take damage from a Hostile creature that you can see, you can take a Reaction to gain 1 Provoked Point. When you hit a creature with a melee attack with a weapon or Unarmed Strike, you can spend a number of Provoked Points equal to half your Rage Damage bonus (round up). For each Provoked Point you spend, the attack deals one additional damage die for the weapon or Unarmed Strike of the same damage type.
You can have a number of Provoked Points equal to your Rage Damage bonus, and all unspent Provoked Points are lost when your Rage ends.

entries.name: Wild Strength
entries: When you take the Attack Action, you can forgo one of your attacks to make a wild swing that threatens all nearby foes. Each creature of your choice within your weapon's reach must make a Dexterity saving throw against a DC equal to 8 plus your Proficiency Bonus plus your Strength modifier. On a failed save, the creature takes damage as though hit by a single melee weapon attack with the weapon you used for this swing.

subclassFeature.name: Dominant of Will
entries: When you enter your Rage, you choose one Dominant of Will feature. This is in addition to your Strength of One selection. You benefit from both options until your Rage ends.

entries.name: Stoic Dominance
entries: You have Advantage on saving throws against the {@condition Charmed} and {@condition Frightened} conditions.

entries.name: Wrathful Dominance
entries: You have Expertise in Intimidation. In addition, while you are {@condition Restrained} or {@condition Prone}, you do not have Disadvantage on melee weapon attack rolls.

entries.name: Wild Dominance
entries: You can take the Dash Action as a Bonus Action. When you take the Dash Action this way, Difficult Terrain doesn't cost you extra movement for the rest of that turn.

subclassFeature.name: Stand Unbound
entries: The more enemies press you, the more violently you answer.

entries.name: Violent Response
entries: While your Rage is active, when a creature you can see forces you to make a saving throw or makes an attack roll against you, you can use your Reaction to mark that creature until the end of your next turn.

While the creature is marked in this way, it is Vulnerable to the next melee weapon attack you hit it with. When you hit that marked creature with a melee weapon attack, the attack deals maximum damage, and the mark ends.
You can use this feature once per Rage.

entries.name: Improved Strength of One
entries: When there are three enemies within 5 feet of you, you score a Critical Hit on a 17, 18, 19, or 20 on the d20 with melee attacks using a weapon or Unarmed Strike.

subclassFeature.name: Reckoning of Choice
entries: When you enter your Rage, you choose one Reckoning of Choice feature. This is in addition to both a Strength of One option and a Dominant of Will option. You benefit from all three options until your Rage ends.

entries.name: Stoic Reckoning
entries: When you use Reckless Attack, you gain Resistance to one damage type of your choice until the start of your next turn, and you are immune to the Stunned condition until the start of your next turn.

entries.name: Wrathful Reckoning
entries: If you use Reckless Attack or Brutal Strike and miss, you can take a Bonus Action to make another melee attack with a weapon or Unarmed Strike with the same weapon or Unarmed Strike against the same target.

entries.name: Wild Reckoning
entries: While you are raging, you can use your Action to make a single melee weapon attack against a creature you can see within your reach. On a hit, the attack deals maximum damage, and the target must make a Constitution saving throw against a DC equal to 8 + your Proficiency Bonus + your Strength modifier. On a failed save, the target is {@condition Stunned} for 1 minute. At the end of each of its turns, the target can make another Constitution saving throw, ending the Stunned condition on itself on a success.

subclassFeature.name: College of the Seers
entries: The ancient order of seers, the völv, examines the children of the raiding clans in search of individuals with the nascent ability to read the runes and connect with the primal forces of the world. Unfortunately, only a few have sufficient gifts to become seers. The others are sent back to their clans after being trained to compose music, sing songs, collect stories, and watch. Many become Bards of the College of the Seers.

This Bard is both a storyteller and a manipulator, capable of playing off both sides in a conflict and coming out the winner. The latter they do in the form of curses that weigh heavily on the minds of the afflicted, bending them to the skald's will.

subclassFeature.name: Bonus Proficiencies
entries: You gain proficiency with Martial Weapons and Training with Medium Armor. You also gain a skill of your choice.

subclassFeature.name: Bestow Fate
entries: As a Magic Action, you target a creature you can see or hear within 30 feet of you as your mark. When you do, you expend one use of Bardic Inspiration, and the creature must make a Charisma saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, choose one of the following fates to impose on the creature for 1 minute:

items: Clumsy. Subtract a roll of your Bardic Inspiration die from the first attack roll the creature makes on each of its turns.
Feeble. Subtract a roll of your Bardic Inspiration die from one saving throw the creature makes before the effect ends (no action required). After doing so, the effect ends.

Slow. The creature's Speed is reduced by 5 feet × the result of your Bardic Inspiration die (minimum Speed 5 feet). At the end of each of the creature's turns, reroll your Bardic Inspiration die to determine the new reduction.

entries: This effect ends early if you use this feature to mark a different creature, if you have the {@condition Incapacitated} condition, or if the target has the {@condition Unconscious} condition or dies.

subclassFeature.name: Enduring Inspiration
entries: You learn two additional fates that you can apply with your Bestow Fate feature:

items: Bold. Add a roll of your Bardic Inspiration die to the first ability check the creature makes on each of its turns.
Sturdy. Add a roll of your Bardic Inspiration die to the first saving throw the creature makes on each of its turns.

entries: In addition, you can bind the fate of multiple creatures. When you take the Magic Action to use Bestow Fate, you can target 2 creatures instead of one and expend one use of Bardic Inspiration for each.

subclassFeature.name: Potent Fate
entries: When a roll from your Bestow Fate feature uses your Bardic Inspiration die, you can reroll that die. You must use the second result. You can do this once per turn.
Additionally, when a creature affected by your Bestow Fate makes an attack roll, saving throw, or ability check, you can use your Reaction to force that creature to reroll that roll.
You can decide to use this feature after the creature rolls, but before the DM tells you whether the roll succeeds or fails.

subclassFeature.name: Discovery Domain Spells
entries: With their connections to the gods of the Stone Court, Clerics are important contributors to raiding life. The Discovery Domain concerns itself with sailing, exploring, and seizing the riches to be found.

Your connection to this divine domain ensures you always have certain spells ready. When you reach a Cleric level specified in the Discovery Domain Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

entries.caption: Discovery Domain Spells
rows: {@spell Augury}, {@spell Expeditious Retreat}, {@spell Fog Cloud}, {@spell Pass without Trace}

subclassFeature.name: Expert Mariner
entries: You are trained for long travel, navigation, and fighting across coasts, rivers, and open water.

entries.name: Bonus Proficiencies
entries: You gain proficiency with Martial Weapons, Cartographer's Tools, and Navigator's Tools.

entries.name: Eye of the Navigator
entries: When someone makes a History, Survival, or Perception check to locate or learn where a place is, you can choose to give them a +5 bonus to their roll. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom Modifier, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

entries.name: Powerful Swimmer
entries: You have a Swim Speed equal to your Speed, and you can hold your breath for twice as long as normal.

subclassFeature.name: Channel Divinity: Drowned Breath
entries: When you hit a creature with a melee attack, you can expend a use of your Channel Divinity. The target takes an additional {@damage 1d8} Necrotic damage and makes a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failure, the target becomes cursed for 1 minute and cannot regain Hit Points unless it's underwater; it can only breathe underwater, and takes {@damage 1d8} Necrotic damage at the start of each of its turns outside the water from suffocation. A creature that is Immune to the Exhaustion condition does not take this damage.

subclassFeature.name: Drowning Grip
entries: You can now activate your Drowned Breath by expending a use of Channel Divinity when a creature fails a saving throw against one of your spells.
In addition, a creature affected by Drowned Breath cannot cast spells requiring a Verbal component.

subclassFeature.name: Surveyor of the Depths
entries: You gain the ability to breathe underwater, and your Swim Speed doubles.
You always have the {@spell Tsunami|OotDLREHH} spell prepared. You can also expend a use of Channel Divinity to cast it without expending a spell slot.

subclassFeature.name: Circle of the Devourer
entries: Under the deep, ever-stretching darkness of the long northern winters, the raiders of the Knattle clan have survived, even thrived, where no other dare. Here Druids have long connected with the primal world, and some rare few have touched the true essence of Grimnir.

You are one of these hardy, pragmatic Druids. The few, the weak, must perish to nourish the many. And so, you have learned to wrestle the spirits of the lands to transform your own body in various, and often unpredictable ways. You become the defender when threatened, the hunter when starving, and the devourer when assaulted.

subclassFeature.name: Primal Protection
entries: The primal spirits exert their powers to protect you. If you are hit by an attack, you may use a Reaction to roll on the Primal Protection table to determine a defensive effect.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom Modifier, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Short or Long Rest.

entries.caption: Primal Protection
rows: Protruding Spines. Jagged spines burst from your body. Each creature within 5 feet of you takes {@damage 2d4} plus your Wisdom modifier Piercing damage and is pushed 5 feet away from you. The spines then retract.
Bulbous Shell. Your skin hardens into a thick, mottled shell. You gain a +3 bonus to AC until the end of your next turn. If this increased AC would cause the triggering attack to miss you, it does.

Abyssal Glare. Your eyes become glowing purple orbs until the end of your next turn. Whenever a creature deals damage to you, including the triggering attack, it takes Psychic damage equal to twice your Wisdom modifier.
Aberrant Flesh. Your flesh warps and knits itself back together. You regain {@dice 2d4} plus your Wisdom Modifier Hit Points immediately after taking the triggering damage.

subclassFeature.name: Primal Arm
entries: As a Bonus Action, you can expend one use of Wild Shape to transform one of your arms. This transformation lasts for 1 hour, or until you dismiss it as a Bonus Action.
Choose one of the following natural weapons. Each is treated as a Simple weapon with which you are proficient. You use your Wisdom modifier for its attack and damage rolls.

items: Bone Club. Melee Attack Roll: Reach 5 ft. Hit: {@dice 1d8} plus Wisdom modifier Bludgeoning damage. The target must make a Strength saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, the target is Knocked {@condition Prone}.
Bladed Claw. Melee Attack Roll: Reach 5 ft. Hit: {@dice 2d6} plus Wisdom modifier Slashing damage.

Poisonous Barbs. Ranged Attack Roll: Range 30/60 ft. Hit: {@dice 1d8} plus Wisdom modifier Piercing damage. The target must make a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, the target is {@condition Poisoned} until the end of its next turn. A creature Poisoned in this way cannot regain Hit Points.

entries: When you take the Attack Action, you can make one additional attack with your Primal Arm weapon.

subclassFeature.name: Enhanced Senses
entries: You may use a Bonus Action to gain an additional sense. You may only have one of the following active at one time:

items: You gain Darkvision out to a range of 120 feet.
You gain Blindsight out to a range of 10 feet.
You gain Tremorsense out to a range of 30 feet.

entries: This feature ends if you have the {@condition Unconscious} condition.

subclassFeature.name: Primal Expertise
entries: When you use Primal Protection, you choose the effect instead of rolling.

subclassFeature.name: Marauder
entries: All raiders seek glory in battle and the spoils that come from a life full of successful raids. Yet only a few live long enough to achieve these aims. A Marauder demonstrates leadership via small skirmishes at first and slowly they build upon their reputation.

The Marauder understands how to control any battlefield they find themselves upon, from the deck of a ship being tossed by a foul storm to the wind-tossed tundra of the north. They minimize their own losses while inflicting great damage upon their enemies.

subclassFeature.name: Break the Line
entries: You can take a Bonus Action to make an Unarmed Strike using the Shove option. If you have a Shield equipped or the creature has the {@condition Prone} condition, it has Disadvantage on the saving throw.

If you shove a creature and push it, you can push it 10 feet instead of 5 feet, and move with the creature horizontally without provoking Opportunity Attacks, remaining within 5 feet of it at the end of your movement.

subclassFeature.name: Withdraw
entries: While wielding a Shield, you can take a Reaction to reduce the damage of an attack by half your Fighter level (rounded down) plus your Constitution modifier (minimum of 1).

subclassFeature.name: Breaker's Charge
entries: As a Bonus Action, you may spend one use of your Second Wind to move in a straight line up to a distance equal to your Speed. Each creature whose size is one category larger than yours or smaller, and whose space you enter during this movement, must make a Strength saving throw. The DC equals 8 plus your Proficiency Bonus plus your Strength modifier.

On a failed save, the creature takes Bludgeoning damage equal to your Strength Modifier and the creature has the {@condition Prone} condition and is pushed 5 feet to the side of your path. On a successful save, your movement for this action immediately ends.

subclassFeature.name: Rampage
entries: Whenever you or an ally within 10 feet of you reduces a creature to 0 Hit Points with an attack, that creature can take a Bonus Action before the end of the current turn to move up to half its Speed and make one attack.

subclassFeature.name: Enhanced Rampage
entries: The range of your Rampage feature increases to 30 feet. In addition, a creature that makes the Rampage Bonus Action attack can roll {@dice 1d6} and add the result to the attack roll it makes for that attack.

subclassFeature.name: End the Threat
entries: As a Bonus Action, you may spend one use of your Second Wind to command your allies to focus their assault on a single foe. Choose one creature you can see. Each ally within 30 feet of you who can hear you can use its Reaction to move up to half its Speed and make one attack against the chosen target.

subclassFeature.name: Way of the Wanderer
entries: The Way of the Wanderer is a legendary path followed by only one monk in the world at any time. Chosen by fate, the Wanderer walks alone, guided by strange visions and an instinctive sense of destiny's shifting threads. They answer to no clan or god, acting as the unseen counterbalance that prevents the world from tipping into chaos.

They serve no clan and swear no oath to any god. To a Wanderer, fate is a woven cord, and every choice plucks at its strands. Balance is not peace, nor is it gentleness. It is the willingness to act when others hesitate, and to accept that even righteous deeds carry hidden costs.

subclassFeature.name: Solo Lifestyle
entries: Used to traveling alone you have proficiency in one musical instrument of your choice. In addition, you have proficiency in Survival.

subclassFeature.name: Path of Fate
entries: Your choices tug at the strands of destiny, shaping each battle toward order or mayhem.
When you roll Initiative, choose one of three styles: Order, Balance, or Mayhem. You gain that style's benefits for the duration of the combat.
Every time you roll Initiative in the future, you follow the following restrictions:

items: If your previous style was Balance, you may choose Order or Mayhem.
If your previous style was Order or Mayhem, you must choose that same style or Balance.

entries.name: Order
entries: You can choose to have your Unarmed Strikes deal Cold damage. Creatures of your choice within 30 feet using Unarmed Strikes or weapons with the Finesse property (including yourself) score a Critical Hit on a roll of 18, 19, or 20 on the d20.

entries.name: Balance
entries: You can reroll one d20 Test that you make. You must use the new roll. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier, regaining all uses when you finish a Long Rest.

entries.name: Mayhem
entries: You can choose to have your Unarmed Strikes deal Thunder damage. When using your Deflect Attacks and you spend 1 Focus Point to redirect the damage, you add one Martial Arts die in Thunder damage to the damage dealt. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier, regaining all uses when you finish a Long Rest.

entries.name: Weather
entries: When you enter battle, fate reshapes the world. For a mile around you, the weather changes to match your chosen style. Mayhem unleashes violent storms of wind, lightning, and pelting rain or ice. Order brings crushing stillness, with no wind, harsh sunlight, and total silence as even animals refuse to make sound. Only in Balance does the world behave as nature intends. This change in weather lasts for an hour.

subclassFeature.name: Forked Destiny
entries: You can spend Focus Points on powers associated with either Order or Mayhem.

items: Final Punch. As a Bonus Action after hitting a creature with an attack, you can spend 3 Focus points to force it to make a Charisma saving throw or be transported to a harmless demiplane. While there, the target has the {@condition Incapacitated} condition. At the end of its next turn, the target reappears in the space it left or in the nearest unoccupied space if that space is occupied. You can't use this power again until you roll Initiative.

Twist of Fate. When a creature within 5 feet takes damage from a melee attack, you can spend 2 Focus points and use your Reaction to reduce the damage by your Monk level plus your Wisdom modifier. Your Unarmed Strikes deal an extra {@dice 1d6} Radiant damage until the end of your next turn.
Lightning Leap. As a Bonus Action, you can spend 2 Focus points to teleport up to 60 feet to a space you can see. Your Unarmed Strikes this turn deal an extra {@dice 1d6} Lightning damage.

Steal Fate. As a Bonus Action, you can spend 4 Focus points to swap Initiative positions with a creature you can see within 60 feet. You can't use this power again until you roll Initiative. A creature can't take two turns in a round as a result of this effect, and if a creature would lose its turn this round as a result of this effect, it takes its turn immediately after your turn this round.

subclassFeature.name: Chosen in Motion
entries: When you roll Initiative, if you choose Mayhem or Order, you gain special abilities for 1 minute.

entries.name: Order Ability
entries: You have Resistance to Cold and Radiant damage. Difficult terrain does not affect you; your Speed increases by 10 feet; you do not provoke Opportunity Attacks.

entries.name: Mayhem Ability
entries: You have Resistance to Lightning and Thunder damage. You have a Fly Speed equal to your Speed.

subclassFeature.name: World-Thread Mastery
entries: While you are in the Balance style, you can spend 1 Focus Point as a Bonus Action to change to either the Order or Mayhem style.

subclassFeature.name: Oath of the Slain
entries: The Slain are Paladins that have embraced their inevitable death, emulating their Vanir hero, Thonir, and intending to serve him in their afterlife. They enforce clan law and often serve as executioners, ridding the raiders of criminals and the corrupt. The Slain believe the laws they follow are above those of the living.

items: Glory. Seek great deeds worthy of the gods.
Incorruptible. Clan law supersedes all earthly loyalties.
Death Is the Beginning. Your end is a passage into divine service.
Prepare for the End. Use wealth and power to strengthen Grimnir before Ragnarok.

subclassFeature.name: Oath Spells
entries: You gain Oath Spells at the listed levels and always have them prepared.

entries.name: Fight to the Last
entries: You can use one use of your Channel Divinity as a Magic Action to restore Hit Points to creatures of your choice within 15 feet. You can restore a total number of Hit Points, divided as you choose, equal to twice your Paladin level. If a creature is at 0 Hit Points when it receives this healing, it regains twice the amount you choose to give it.

entries.name: Mark of the Executioner
entries: You can use one use of your Channel Divinity as a Bonus Action to mark one creature you can see for execution for 1 minute. While the mark lasts, your attack rolls against the creature score a Critical Hit on a roll of 18-20 on the d20. The effect ends early if you become {@condition Incapacitated} or if you mark another creature.

subclassFeature.name: Claim of the Vanir
entries: Your soul refuses to rise as undead: no effect or creature can cause you to return to life as an undead creature.

subclassFeature.name: Aura of the Executioner
entries: You and your allies gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls while in your Aura of Protection.

subclassFeature.name: A Glorious Sacrifice
entries: When you are reduced to 0 Hit Points but not killed outright, you can use your Reaction to have a number of Hit Points equal to twice your Paladin level instead. When you do this, you take an extra turn as soon as the current turn ends.

During this extra turn, you can only move up to your Speed, take the Attack Action, and use your Bonus Action to cast a Paladin spell that has a casting time of a Bonus Action. At the end of this extra turn, you take Radiant damage equal to twice your Paladin level.
You can't use this feature again until you finish a Long Rest.

subclassFeature.name: Justice Delivered
entries: As a Bonus Action, you undergo a divine transformation, granting the benefits below for 1 minute or until you end them (no action required).

entries.name: Impervious Flesh
entries: You have Advantage on saving throws against spells and magical effects.

entries.name: Might of the Gods
entries: When a creature within 10 feet of you hits a target with a melee attack, you can use your Reaction to make one melee weapon attack against that target. You have Advantage on the attack roll.

entries.name: Aura of the Worthy
entries: Your Aura of the Executioner now grants you and your allies a bonus to attack rolls equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum bonus of +1). In addition, you and your allies have Immunity to the {@condition Charmed} condition while in your Aura of Protection. If a Charmed ally enters the aura, that condition has no effect on that ally while there.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest. You can also restore your use of it by expending the use of one level 5 spell slot (no action required).

subclassFeature.name: Wolf Rider
entries: Wolves have returned to Grimnir. They choose riders from the Whar clan; and in doing so, reshape the clan's power. As one of these chosen, you ride in Hel's name, part of a pack, never alone, seeking glory, honor, and the favor of the Lady of the Dead. The wolf decides. The clans must follow.

subclassFeature.name: Wolf Companion
entries: A Grimnir Wolf chooses you as its rider. It is friendly to you and your allies, and it obeys your commands. See its game statistics in the accompanying {@creature Grimnir Wolf|OotDLREHH} stat block, which uses your Proficiency Bonus (PB) in several places.

entries.name: Your Wolf in Combat
entries: In combat, the wolf acts during your turn. It can move and use its Reaction on its own, but the only action it takes is the Dodge action unless you take a Bonus Action to command it to take an action in its stat block or some other action. You can also sacrifice one of your attacks when you take the Attack action to command the wolf to take the Bite action. If you have the {@condition Incapacitated} condition, the wolf acts on its own and isn't limited to the Dodge action.

entries.name: Bonded Soul
entries: You and your wolf share limited telepathy out to 120 feet. The wolf can move stealthily at a normal pace while within 10 feet of you.

entries.name: Bonded Commands
entries: When you cast the {@spell Hunter's Mark} spell without expending a spell slot or move the mark to a new creature, you can command your Grimnir Wolf as part of the same Bonus Action. In addition, you gain certain benefits when you give your wolf the Dodge or Help commands.

items: Dodge: If the wolf takes the Dodge action and remains within 10 feet of you, attack rolls against you have Disadvantage until the start of your next turn.
Help: When the wolf uses the Help action to assist you in attacking a creature, your next attack against that creature scores a Critical Hit on a roll of 18-20 on the d20.

entries.name: If Your Wolf Dies
entries: You must bury its remains. If you do not have access to its remains you must spend an hour carving a totem and bury that instead. After you finish a Long Rest, it returns to life at full Hit Points from beneath the earth.

subclassFeature.name: Woodland Rider
entries: You can ride your wolf as a mount without a saddle.

entries.name: Wolf and Rider Defense
entries: While you and your wolf are within 5 feet of one another and neither is Incapacitated, you each gain a +1 bonus to AC.

entries.name: Mounted Wolf Riding
entries: While mounted on your wolf:

items: When an attack misses you or your wolf, the wolf can use its Reaction to move up to half its Speed. This movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks.
Mounting or dismounting costs 10 feet of movement.
You have Advantage on checks to avoid falling off your mount.

entries.name: Improved Bonded Commands
entries: Your coordination with your wolf deepens, granting additional benefits to your Bonded Commands:

items: Ambush: When your wolf takes the Hide action and you are riding it, if it succeeds, you also have the Invisible condition as if you succeeded the check with the wolf's total.

Aggressive Help: In addition to the Bonded Command benefits of commanding your wolf to use the Help action, if your attack hits the creature, the wolf can use its Reaction to make one Bite attack against that creature.
Near Shot: You don't have Disadvantage on ranged weapon attacks made within 5 feet of a creature, as long as your wolf is within 10 feet of the target.

subclassFeature.name: Dangerous Beast
entries: You and your wolf strike together with coordination.

entries.name: Lethal Pack
entries: If your wolf uses the Help action to aid you, your next attack against that target scores a Critical Hit on a 17-20. If you use the Help action to aid the wolf, its next attack scores a Critical Hit on a 15-20.

entries.name: Wolf Aspect
entries: Your wolf gains one aspect. You can change the chosen aspect after a Long Rest.

items: Frost Wolf: Your wolf adds {@dice 1d4} Frost damage to each of its attacks. Once per turn, the wolf can reroll its damage and use either result.
Forest Wolf: The wolf and all allies within 15 feet have Advantage on Initiative rolls.

subclassFeature.name: Defend the Pack
entries: Your bond turns instinct into protection.

entries.name: Favored Bond
entries: When your wolf is about to be reduced to 0 Hit Points or killed, you can expend one use of your Favored Enemy to change its Hit Points to be 1 instead or prevent it from dying (no action required).

entries.name: Pack Cover
entries: While Concentrating on {@spell Hunter's Mark}, you and your wolf have the benefits of Half Cover.

subclassFeature.name: True Believer
entries: Cornered and desperate, the Rogue muttered a prayer to Mirgal, the dead Vanir. Against all odds, they survived. Since then, they've kept their faith secret, calling on Mirgal in dire moments. Whether the aid is real or not, they believe, and that belief is all that matters.

subclassFeature.name: False Gods
entries: Your devotion and secrecy sharpen your understanding of other faiths. You gain proficiency in one of the following skills: Deception, History, or Religion.

subclassFeature.name: Spellcasting
entries: You gain the ability to cast spells from the Cleric list.

entries.name: Cantrips
entries: You know three cantrips of your choice from the Cleric spell list.

entries.name: Spell Slots
entries: The True Believer Spellcasting table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your level 1+ spells. You regain all expended slots when you finish a Long Rest.

entries.name: Prepared Spells of Level 1+
entries: You prepare the list of level 1+ spells that are available for you to cast with this feature. To start, choose three level 1 spells from the Cleric spell list. The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Rogue levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the True Believer Spellcasting table. Whenever that number increases, choose additional spells from the Cleric spell list until the number of spells on your list matches the number on the table. The chosen spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

entries.name: Changing Your Prepared Spells
entries: Whenever you gain a Rogue level, you can replace one spell on your list with another Cleric spell for which you have spell slots.

entries.name: Spellcasting Ability
entries: Intelligence or Wisdom (your choice) is your spellcasting ability for your Cleric spells.

entries.name: Spellcasting Focus
entries: You can use a Holy Symbol as a Spellcasting Focus for your Cleric spells.

subclassFeature.name: Dubious Healing
entries: When you cast a spell that restores Hit Points, you can choose to give the target Temporary Hit Points equal to the amount the spell would have healed instead of restoring any Hit Points.

subclassFeature.name: Wrath of Divinity
entries: When you deal Sneak Attack damage to a creature, you can deal an additional {@damage 3d6} Radiant or Necrotic Damage (your choice).

items: If you choose Radiant, one creature you can see within 60 feet regains Hit Points equal to the bonus damage dealt.
If you choose Necrotic, the target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC or have the {@condition Frightened} condition until the end of your next turn.

entries: You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Dexterity Modifier, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

subclassFeature.name: Push Your Luck
entries: As a Magic Action, make a DC 15 ability check using your Wisdom.

items: Success: You regain all expended spell slots and all expended uses of Wrath of Divinity.
Failure: You gain one level of Exhaustion. The next time you use this feature, you have Advantage on the check.

entries: You can use this feature once, and you regain the use of it when you finish a Long Rest.

subclassFeature.name: Misplaced Soul
entries: In your dreams you remember a vast and strange place that you have come to believe is where you originated--or where you were kept until needed. You have memories of other souls, like yourself, lingering in that domain. You have the power to summon these souls.

subclassFeature.name: Companions from the Before
entries: You can use a Bonus Action to summon a {@creature Misplaced Soul|OotDLREHH} in an unoccupied space within 10 feet of you. You can have only one Misplaced Soul at a time.

The Misplaced Soul uses a special stat block (provided below). When you summon it, it gains additional Hit Points equal to 5 times the number of Sorcery Points you spend. The Misplaced Soul lasts for 10 minutes, until you use a Bonus Action to dismiss it, or until you or the Soul drop to 0 Hit Points.
You can summon a Misplaced Soul a number of times equal to your Charisma Modifier, and you regain all uses when you finish a Long Rest.

subclassFeature.name: Act as One
entries: Your thoughts and the Misplaced Soul's essence flow together.

entries.name: Telepathy
entries: You and the Misplaced Soul can communicate telepathically while you are within 120 feet of each other.

entries.name: Shared Movement and Action
entries: On your turn, you can use a Bonus Action to move the Misplaced Soul up to 30 feet. At the end of this movement, it can take one action of your choice from its stat block.

entries.name: Metamagic: Swap
entries: (1 Sorcery Point.) As part of the same Bonus Action, you can spend 1 Sorcery Point to instantly swap positions with the Misplaced Soul if it is within 30 feet of you. This movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks.

subclassFeature.name: Soul Bound Commands
entries: You gain the ability to spend Sorcery Points to have your Misplaced Soul perform specific actions.

entries.name: Metamagic: Thrash
entries: (1 Sorcery Point.) You may use a Bonus Action to have your Misplaced Soul use its Thrash attack. This can also be done as part of the Bonus Action you use to summon a Misplaced Soul.

entries.name: Metamagic: Reduce Harm
entries: (2 Sorcery Points.) You may have your Misplaced Soul use its Reduce Harm as a Reaction when a creature within 5 feet of it is hit by an attack.

subclassFeature.name: The Imagined Offense
entries: You gain additional Soul Bound Commands:

entries.name: Metamagic: Consume
entries: (1 Sorcery Point.) You absorb the Misplaced Soul in a burst of soulstuff. You regain Hit Points equal to its current Hit Points, and the Misplaced Soul vanishes.

entries.name: Metamagic: Improved Thrash
entries: (1 Sorcery Point.) Your Misplaced Soul's Thrash now deals {@damage 2d12} plus your Charisma modifier Psychic damage, instead of {@damage 2d8}.

subclassFeature.name: Dreams Made Real
entries: When you summon a Misplaced Soul, you can spend additional Sorcery Points to grant it special traits. These traits last until the Soul disappears.

entries.name: Metamagic: Magic Resistance
entries: (1 Sorcery Point.) You give the Misplaced Soul the Magic Resistance trait (see accompanying stat block).

entries.name: Metamagic: Regeneration
entries: (2 Sorcery Points.) You give the Misplaced Soul the Regeneration trait (see accompanying stat block).

entries.name: Metamagic: Reality
entries: (4 Sorcery Points.) The Misplaced Soul that you create loses the Invisibility trait. It gains the Rend Ranged Attack and the Magic Resistance and Regeneration traits. If you become Incapacitated or are reduced to 0 Hit Points while this Misplaced Soul exists, roll 1d20. If you roll a 1 or 2 the Misplaced Soul becomes a real creature that persists. They are under the DM's control and have the stat block of an {@creature Archmage}. Their disposition is Friendly towards you.
Once a Misplaced Soul becomes a real creature in this manner, this effect won't transform a Misplaced Soul into a real creature again until 1 year has passed.

subclassFeature.name: Patron: The Ironwood
entries: Your patron is a powerful ironheart tree, a patriarch or matriarch of one of the great ironwood forests. These trees originated from the old world, the Lost Lands. Their motives are unknown, not even to those who claim to have much knowledge of them.

subclassFeature.name: Expanded Spell List
entries: The magic of your patron ensures you always have certain spells ready; when you reach a Warlock level specified in the Ironwood Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

subclassFeature.name: Vitality of the Ironwood
entries: Your patron gifts you a Heartseed, a Tiny organic focus that pulses with slow, ancient life. It is your spellcasting focus. If you lose it, you can perform a 1-hour ritual to grow a new one.

entries.name: Vitality
entries: While touching the Heartseed, you can use a Bonus Action to awaken the patron's vitality within you for 10 minutes. Until the effect ends:

items: You gain Temporary Hit Points equal to your Warlock level plus your Charisma Modifier (minimum of 2).
Your Speed increases by 5 feet.

entries: Using this feature again ends the previous use. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma Modifier, regaining all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

subclassFeature.name: Armor of the Ironwood
entries: During a Long or Short Rest, you can grow a suit of living armor called Ironwood Armor, using your Heartseed. Only you can wear this armor, and you have the training to use it. If you grow another Ironwood Armor, the previous one vanishes. While wearing this armor, you have Training with Shields.

entries.name: Ironwood Armor
entries: Armor Class = 10 + Dex modifier + Cha modifier.
Resistance to Bludgeoning damage.
Choose one of the following forms each time you grow the armor:

items: Mantle of Leaves. You have Advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks. Your Speed increases by an additional 5 feet.
Unbreakable Branches. Attack rolls against you can't score Critical Hits.

subclassFeature.name: Tree Passage
entries: You gain the ability to enter a tree and move from inside it to inside another tree within 500 feet. Both trees must be at least the same size as you. You must use 5 feet of movement to enter a tree. You instantly know the location of all other trees within 500 feet and, as part of the move used to enter the tree, can either pass into one of those trees or step out of the tree you're in. You appear in a spot of your choice within 5 feet of the destination tree, using another 5 feet of movement. If you have no movement left, you appear within 5 feet of the tree you entered. When you exit one of two things happen:

items: Intelligent Tree. If the tree has an Intelligence score, roll a number of d6 equal to your Charisma Modifier. You regain Hit Points equal to the total.

Nonintelligent Tree. If the tree has no Intelligence score, it explodes. All creatures of your choice within 15 feet must make a Dexterity saving throw (using your Warlock spell save DC). Failure: {@damage 5d6} Piercing damage. Success: Half damage.

entries: You can use Tree Passage a number of times equal to your Charisma Modifier, regaining all uses on a Short or Long Rest.

subclassFeature.name: Colossus of the Ironwood
entries: While wearing your Ironwood Armor, you can use a Bonus Action to transform into a Large size, bark-covered humanoid if you are in a space large enough. This transformation lasts for 10 minutes, or until you end it early as a Bonus Action, or if you die. You have the following benefits while transformed:

items: You gain Temporary Hit Points equal to five times your Warlock level.
You have Advantage on attack rolls that you make with Simple and Martial weapons.
When you hit a creature with a weapon attack, that attack deals an extra {@damage 3d6} Force damage. You can deal this extra damage no more than once on each turn.

entries: You must finish a Long Rest to use this feature again. You may also regain its use by expending the use of one of your Mystic Arcanum (no action required).

subclassFeature.name: Cohesion of the Primal
entries: Primal Wizards carve their spells into their own flesh, weaving ink with ancient power older than Grimnir itself. They chase the echoes of this first world; an early, primeval, state of the current world. Some, called Dreamers, seek hidden truths in those echoes, believing the primal past holds the key to saving Grimnir from the fate of the Lost Lands. Others, the Seekers, hunt and destroy artifacts, lost tomes, and any mage reckless enough to pursue such forbidden knowledge.

subclassFeature.name: Primal Ink
entries: Your body is your spellbook. You are proficient with Calligrapher's Supplies and inscribe your spells as shifting tattoos across your skin. Copying a spell into your tattoos takes twice as long but costs half as much gold as copying into a spellbook. Your tattoo-spellbook cannot be destroyed while you live. Your tattoos do not count as a spellcasting focus.

During a Long Rest, your tattoos rearrange, allowing you to choose which spells to prepare. You can surface unprepared tattoos visibly to allow copying or transcription. You must have an Arcane Focus to prepare spells.

subclassFeature.name: Arcane Intentions
entries: Choose one intention: Dreamer or Seeker. Dreamers glimpse fragments of possible futures, while Seekers hunt those who wield magic. The intention that you choose determines the features that are available to you from this subclass.
You may change your intention at levels 6, 10, and 14. You gain proficiency with Light Armor.

entries.name: Dreamer
entries: As a Bonus Action, you replace one prepared spell with another spell of the same level or lower from your spellbook. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum once), regaining all uses on a Long Rest.

entries.name: Seeker
entries: As a Magic Action, you expend a spell slot to sense the direction of every creature with the Spellcasting or Innate Spellcasting trait within 1 mile of you for 2 hours. Once you use this feature, you cannot do so again until you finish a Long Rest.
You gain Expertise in Investigation.

subclassFeature.name: Foresaying
entries: You can better see the connections between the past and the future.

entries.name: Dreamer: Stored Foresight
entries: When you cast a Wizard spell of level 5 or lower using a spell slot with a casting time of an Action or longer and a range of Self, you can store it instead of gaining its effects. You can later cast the stored spell as a Bonus Action without expending a spell slot or consuming components. You can store only one spell at a time. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier, and regain all uses when you finish a Long Rest. Any stored spell fades at the end of a Long Rest.

entries.name: Seeker: Disrupt Spellcasting
entries: When you hit a creature with a melee or ranged weapon attack, you may use a Bonus Action to force it to make an Intelligence saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, the creature cannot cast spells or take the Magic action until the end of your next turn. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier, regaining all uses on a Long Rest.

entries.name: Dreamer: Master Foresayer
entries: When you activate your Stored Foresight spell as a Bonus Action, you can roll {@dice 1d4}. On a 4, the stored spell is not expended.

entries.name: Seeker: Advanced Disruption
entries: When a spell with a single target affects you or an ally within 10 feet, you may use your Reaction and expend a spell slot equal to or higher than the spell's level. If you do, the spell fails. Once you use this feature, you cannot do so again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

subclassFeature.name: Cord & Curse
entries: You have gained expertise in trials of arcane combat.

entries.name: Dreamer: Primeval Call
entries: When you lose Concentration on a spell as a result of taking damage, you can take a Reaction to cast the {@spell Summon Beast} spell at a level equal to the spell you lost Concentration on without expending a spell slot or requiring Concentration. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

entries.name: Seeker: Spell Immunity Tattoo
entries: Choose 3 spells from your spellbook. You are Immune to these spells. You can change one of these spells for another spell from your spellbook when you finish a Long Rest or by taking a Magic action and expending a spell slot equal to the level of the spell you wish to become Immune to.

subclassFeature.name: Herculean Path
entries: Some individuals are born with seemingly impossible strength, exhibiting rippling muscles even before they learn to speak or walk. As one such individual, you know that strength is what determines one's worth in the world: strength to crush your enemies--and to impress your allies. Your incredible strength allows you to accomplish Herculean feats that will leave your foes wailing in anguish.

subclassFeature.name: Precocious Wrestler
entries: You are a natural bruiser. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Mighty Arms
entries: You can make one Unarmed Strike as a Bonus Action while your Rage is active.

entries.name: Iron Grip
entries: While you are grappling a creature, you can wield a Two-Handed weapon with your free hand. In addition, while your Rage is active, you can use the Grapple or Shove option of your Unarmed Strike against Huge or smaller creatures.

entries.name: Natural Vigor
entries: You gain Expertise in Athletics. If you already had Proficiency in Athletics, you can gain Proficiency in another skill from the Barbarian skill list.

subclassFeature.name: Mighty Marksman
entries: You mix might with skill to enter the arena of ranged combat. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Great Bow
entries: Longbows have the Finesse property when you wield them.

entries.name: Thunderous Shot
entries: When you hit a creature with a Ranged attack using a weapon, you can imbue the attack with concussive force. Roll a number of d8s equal to your Rage damage bonus and add them together. Each creature within a 10-foot-radius Sphere centered on the target takes Thunder damage equal to the total rolled and has the {@condition Prone} condition if it is Large or smaller.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest unless you expend a use of your Rage (no action required) to restore your use of it.

subclassFeature.name: Herculean Rage
entries: Your rage takes on a legendary intensity. While your Rage is active, you can add your Rage Damage bonus to the save DC of the Grapple and Shove options when you make an Unarmed Strike, and you have Immunity to the {@condition Frightened} condition. If you're Frightened when you enter your Rage, the condition ends.

subclassFeature.name: Earthshaker
entries: When you activate your Rage, you can unleash such power that the very earth trembles beneath you. This form lasts for 1 minute or until you drop to 0 Hit Points. Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest.
While in this form, you gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Quaking Steps
entries: Once per turn when you move at least 5 feet, an intense tremor rips through the ground in a 40-foot Emanation originating from you. Each creature of your choice in the area must make a Dexterity saving throw (DC 8 plus your Strength modifier and Proficiency bonus). On a failed save, a creature has the {@condition Prone} condition, and its Concentration is broken.

entries.name: Seismic Strike
entries: The first target you hit with a melee weapon or an Unarmed Strike each turn takes an extra {@dice 1d6} Bludgeoning damage. Whenever you hit an object, the hit is a Critical Hit.

subclassFeature.name: College of Epic Poetry
entries: Bards of the College of Epic Poetry are devoted to the creation of a singular masterpiece in the tradition of epic poets. They spend their early years studying philosophy and the arts, arming themselves with the aesthetic languages to capture the splendor of great deeds. Eventually, they seek out great conflicts and the heroes within, their poetry making the bard an eternal witness to the glorious and dramatic lives of immortals.

subclassFeature.name: Epic Verses
entries: Dramatic moments inspire you to compose and declaim your epic poem, adding to the spectacle. When one of the events listed below occurs by chance (i.e. your party cannot deliberately force them to happen through repetition), you can use your Reaction and expend one use of Bardic Inspiration to generate the event's listed effect.
When you do, your Verse count increases by 1. Your Verse count is a cumulative number that increases over the lifetime of your character.

items: Comedy. A creature you can see or hear rolls a natural 1 on a d20 Test. Choose a number of creatures within 30 feet of yourself, up to a number equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one creature). Those creatures have Disadvantage on their next d20 Test.

Excellence. A creature you can see or hear rolls a natural 20 on a d20 Test. Choose a number of creatures within 30 feet of yourself, up to a number equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one creature). Those creatures have Advantage on their next d20 Test.

Irony. An ally misses an attack or fails a saving throw after rolling a Bardic Inspiration die. One creature of your choice subtracts the number rolled by that ally from their next attack roll or saving throw, whichever comes first.
Tragedy. An ally you can see or hear is reduced to 0 Hit Points by an enemy. Roll a Bardic Inspiration die. That ally gains a number of Hit Points equal to the number rolled.

entries.name: Recording your Poetry
entries: When you increase your Verse count, you may also want to write down what happened and why, so that you can enjoy reading it later. You should also consider assigning an epithet to each of your allies. Epithets are short compound titles like "rosy-cheeked," "strong-willed," or "clear-eyed." Epic poets use epithets to emphasize a character's most distinguished qualities.

subclassFeature.name: Armored Poet
entries: You gain training with Medium armor. In addition, if you are within 5 feet of a creature when it triggers Epic Verses, you do not expend a Bardic Inspiration.

subclassFeature.name: Inspirational Verses
entries: Your epic poem has grown such that it leaves a lasting impression. When a creature gains one of your Bardic Inspiration dice, it also gains one of the following benefits for as long as it has that die.

items: Agility. The creature's Speed is increased by 10 feet. In addition, its movement is unaffected by Difficult Terrain.
Vigor. The creature gains Resistance to one damage type (Bard's choice). In addition, it gains Temporary Hit Points equal to half your Bard level.

Foresight. Requires a Verse count of 15. The creature adds {@dice 1d4} to their Initiative rolls. In addition, when the creature rolls the Bardic Inspiration die, it can treat a roll of 4 or lower as a 5.

Ingenuity. Requires a Verse count of 30. The creature has Advantage on Intelligence and Charisma saving throws. In addition, when the creature rolls a Wisdom saving throw, it can treat a roll of 9 or lower as a 10.

Power. Requires a Verse count of 60. The creature's attack rolls with weapons and Unarmed Strikes can score a Critical Hit on a roll of 19 or 20 on the d20. In addition, when the creature has Advantage on an attack roll, it can reroll one of the dice once.

Protection. Requires a Verse count of 90. When a character with one of your Bardic Inspiration dice would be reduced to 0 hit points, they may choose to roll their Bardic Inspiration die and be reduced to that number of hit points instead. The Bardic Inspiration die is then lost.
Spellheart. Requires a Verse count of 120. The creature's spell save DC and spell attack bonus each increase by +1.

subclassFeature.name: Poetic End
entries: The awe of your peers crowns you a poet of the ages. As a Magic Action, you can end all of your currently ongoing Bardic Inspirations. Each creature that had this inspiration rolls {@dice 1d4 + 1} and can restore a combined number of charges from any trait, feature, or magic item that regains all uses when they take a Long Rest or at dawn equal to the total rolled, excluding the Spellcasting and Mystic Arcanum features. For example, a Paladin who rolled a 3 could restore his or her Paladin's Smite use and two charges of Channel Divinity.

Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a number of Long Rests equal to the number of creatures affected by Poetic End plus 1. Poetic End can't restore uses of features that require more than one Long Rest to recover.

subclassFeature.name: Prophecy Domain
entries: The Prophecy domain focuses on foretelling danger and preventing harmful outcomes. Clerics of this domain are also known as "oracles." Oracles pay special attention to dreams, intuitive thoughts, and hallucinatory visions. They are widely believed to be capable of predicting the future, though their visions are often misinterpreted. They live by the phrase, "know thyself."

Oracles often carry special varieties of incense and holy water with them. The holy water may be boiled to produce vapors, which the oracle inhales in order to enter a trance-like state. During such a trance, the oracle thrashes and wails as they experience flashes of divine insight.

subclassFeature.name: Prophecy Domain Spells
entries: Your power as an oracle gives you access to certain spells. When you reach a Cleric level specified in the Prophecy Domain Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

subclassFeature.name: Channel Divinity: Prophetic Trance
entries: You can use your Channel Divinity to enter A Prophetic Trance. As a Bonus action, you inhale hallucinatory vapors and enter a trance-like state for 10 minutes. For the duration, whenever a creature you can see within 60 feet makes or fails a d20 Test, you can use your Reaction to impose one of the following effects on that test:

items: Treat the d20 roll as a 10.
The creature rerolls the d20 and uses the higher roll.
The creature adds {@dice 1d4} to the result of the d20 Test.

entries: After you use your Reaction in this way, the trance ends unless you choose to gain 1 level of Exhaustion.

subclassFeature.name: Blessing of Foresight
entries: You use spells from the Divination school of magic to protect your allies from future events. Whenever you cast a Divination spell of level 1 or higher using a Spell Slot, choose one creature you can see. That creature gains Temporary Hit Points equal to your Wisdom modifier + your Cleric level.

subclassFeature.name: Visions of Danger
entries: You can experience flashes of foresight that reveal to you when your allies will be harmed, allowing you to react with uncanny speed.

entries.name: Flash of Foresight
entries: When one of your allies takes damage or fails a saving throw, you may use your Reaction to move up to your speed and cast a Divination spell or a spell that restores Hit Points to one creature. The casting time of the spell must be a Reaction, action, or Bonus Action. You may use this feature twice, and you regain any expended uses when you finish a Short or Long Rest.

entries.name: Augury Master
entries: When you use your Channel Divinity to enter a Prophetic Trance, you gain the following additional options that you can apply using your Reaction when a creature you can see within 60 feet makes a d20 Test:

items: The creature rerolls the d20 and uses the lower roll.
The creature subtracts {@dice 1d4} from the result of the d20 Test.

subclassFeature.name: Perfect Foresight
entries: When you use your Channel Divinity to enter a Prophetic Trance, you gain the following additional options that you can apply using your Reaction when a creature you can see within 60 feet makes a d20 Test:

items: Treat the d20 roll as a 2.
Treat the d20 roll as a 19.
The creature rolls {@dice 1d10} and adds the result to the d20 Test.

entries: You can use your Reaction in this way a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier. The trance ends after you use all of these uses unless you choose to gain 1 level of Exhaustion, in which case the trance continues.
Additionally, while you are in the trance:

items: You have Darkvision out to a range of 120 feet.
You can see Invisible creatures and objects.

subclassFeature.name: Circle of Sacrifice
entries: Druids of the Circle of Sacrifice believe that nature connects one to the entire universe, including the stars and the astral void between planes. They know that immutable laws have been set down by the great powers of the universe and that sacrifices must be made to these powers in order to keep the balance. Such sacrifices take the form of great bonfires, wherein fallen creatures are immolated.
Druids who keep the Circle of Sacrifice are sometimes called the Keepers of the Old Ways, and they revere mistletoe as a sacred plant connected to the infinite power of the astral plane.

subclassFeature.name: Circle of Sacrifice Spells
entries: When you reach a Druid level specified in the Circle of Sacrifice Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared. In addition, you know the {@spell Fire Bolt} cantrip. When you roll damage with any of the leveled spells on the Circle of Sacrifice Spells table, add your Wisdom modifier to the damage roll.

subclassFeature.name: Ritual of Sacrifice
entries: Whenever you reduce a creature to 0 Hit Points with Fire damage, you may choose to immolate them as a sacrificial offering. As the creature is engulfed in fire, you and every ally within 60 feet of the immolated creature gain the effects of the {@spell Bless} spell for 1 minute (Concentration is not required).
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier and regain all expended uses when you finish a Short or Long Rest.

subclassFeature.name: Ritual of Mistletoes
entries: You carry a pouch full of mistletoe that you've collected with your sickle. You have sprigs of mistletoe represented by a number of d4s equal to your Wisdom modifier. On your turn, you may use a Bonus Action to expend one of the sprigs of mistletoe and perform one of the following effects:

items: Divining Ritual. You cast the {@spell Detect Magic} spell without expending a spell slot.
Healing Ritual. You cast the {@spell Cure Wounds} spell without expending a spell slot.
Purification Ritual. You cast the {@spell Purify Food and Drink} spell without expending a spell slot.
Song of the Solstice. You cast the {@spell Heroism} spell without expending a spell slot.

entries: Additionally, any time you cast a spell that restores Hit Points, you can expend a number of mistletoe up to your Proficiency Bonus. Roll the mistletoe dice you expend and add the total to the number of Hit Points restored.
You regain all expended sprigs of mistletoe when you finish a Long Rest or if you expend 2 uses of your Wild Shape feature as a Bonus Action to regain all expended uses.

subclassFeature.name: Keeper of the Law
entries: You are initiated into an ancient order of druidic judges who keep and enforce the laws of the cosmos.

entries.name: High Mistletoe
entries: Your sprigs of mistletoe increase to d8s.

entries.name: Sacrificial Offering
entries: On your turn, you can use a Bonus Action to choose one creature that you can see. That creature is marked as a Sacrificial Offering for the next hour. Whenever any of your allies hit that creature with an attack, you may use a Reaction to expend one of your sprigs of mistletoe to roll the die and add the result as Fire Damage. Additionally, whenever a Sacrificial Offering is reduced to 0 Hit Points, you may activate your Ritual of Sacrifice feature on that creature.

subclassFeature.name: Astrological Wisdom
entries: You have studied the stars and memorized the pathways that connect the material plane to the astral plane.

entries.name: Elder Mistletoe
entries: Your sprigs of mistletoe increase to d12s.

entries.name: Burning Omen
entries: When you mark a creature as a Sacrificial Offering or as a Bonus Action on a later turn, you can expend a sprig of mistletoe to empower its effect. Until the start of your next turn, you can use Sacrificial Offering once per turn without taking a Reaction, but still expending a sprig of mistletoe.

entries.name: Stone Circle
entries: You gain access to the {@spell Teleportation Circle} spell and always have it prepared. Additionally, you know the ancient methods used to construct a circle of standing stones. You may spend 8 hours and 1,000 GP to construct a circle of twelve standing stones inscribed with druidic sigils, where each stone is 10 feet tall and weighs 1 ton. This stone circle may be used as a permanent anchor location for the {@spell Teleportation Circle} spell.

subclassFeature.name: Circle of the Wyrm
entries: The Circle of the Wyrm is a secret suborder of the Druids of Oldwoods. Long ago, the silver dragon Balmytria laid a clutch of eggs before going to her death against the Twin Titans. She entrusted the eggs to the druids, and Thylea granted them a vision: guard the clutch until the Unspoken Wake.

After Balmytria fell, the eggs grew cold. Centuries passed, yet the grove endured. One night, a druid dreamed a dream not his own. Drawn to the hidden chamber, he found an egg cracking. As it broke, the soul of a silver dragon poured into him, seeking refuge. He became the first of the Circle of the Wyrm.
The dragon spirit within is never silent. Its instincts and half memories press against the druid's thoughts. Many take a sacred rider, an anchor who helps them with their inner struggle.

subclassFeature.name: Dragon Soul
entries: You know the Draconic language. You have Resistance against Cold damage.

You can bring forth the dragon spirit within. When you assume a Wild Shape form, you can choose to take the form of a {@creature Hatchling Silver Dragon|OotDLREHH} (see accompanying stat block). Your Silver Dragon form follows all the same rules as the Wild Shape form with the following exceptions:

entries.name: Wyrmling
entries: You have no Fly Speed. You do not have the Multiattack action.

subclassFeature.name: Circle of the Wyrm Spells
entries: When you reach a Druid level specified in the Circle of the Wyrm Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared. In addition, you can cast the spells from this feature while you're in a Wild Shape form.

entries.caption: Circle of the Wyrm Spells
rows: {@spell Ray of Frost}, {@spell Ice Knife}, {@spell Zone of Truth}

subclassFeature.name: Sacred Rider
entries: Your experience better attunes you to your dragon body.

entries.name: Maturing Wyrm Spirit
entries: You better attune to your dragon body. You no longer have the Wyrmling portion of your Dragon Soul feature.

entries.name: Natural Partner
entries: In addition, after you finish a Long Rest, you can designate one Medium or smaller creature as your natural partner. This bond lasts until you designate a new creature in this way. While your partner is within 10 feet of you, both of you gain the following benefits:

items: Scales. You have a +1 bonus to AC.
Determination. You have Advantage on Constitution saving throws that you make to maintain Concentration.
Partnership. When your partner is targeted by an attack roll, you can take a Reaction and force the attack to target you instead.

subclassFeature.name: Awakened Legacy
entries: Your shared draconic soul blooms.

entries.name: Mature Form
entries: When you assume a Wild Shape form, you can choose to take the form of a {@creature Juvenile Silver Dragon|OotDLREHH} (see accompanying stat block). Your Silver Dragon form follows all the same rules as the Wild Shape form.

entries.name: Enhanced Attacks
entries: When you Wild Shape into a creature with "Silver Dragon" in its name, you can use your spell save DC instead of the DC listed in the stat block and your spell attack modifier instead of the listed attack bonus.

subclassFeature.name: Rekindled Breath
entries: You can expend a level 4+ spell slot to restore all expended uses of your Cold Breath and Paralyzing Breath. This requires no action. When you use your Cold Breath, it deals extra Cold damage equal to your Druid level.

subclassFeature.name: Dragon Knight
entries: Dragon Knights trace their lineage to the last surviving echoes of the Thylean Dragonlords. Whether born of a forgotten bloodline or trained within a secretive guild, each carries fragments of a martial tradition once practiced atop the backs of dragons. With dragons long vanished, these teachings have evolved over centuries, reshaped to suit the lesser creatures that still roam the world.

Horses, griffons, dire wolves, and stranger beasts respond to a Dragon Knight with uncanny trust, becoming extensions of their rider's will. Yet every Dragon Knight nurtures the same secret hope: to one day ride a dragon.

entries.name: Rider's Flow
entries: Mounting or dismounting a creature costs you only 5 feet of movement, rather than half your Speed.

entries.name: Dragon Knight Techniques
entries: You know two of the mounted techniques of your choice from the Mounted Techniques list below. You learn one additional mounted technique of your choice when you reach Fighter levels 7, 10, and 15.

You can gain the benefits of only one mounted technique each turn. Your mounted techniques can only be used with a controlled mount. You can use mounted techniques a number of times equal to your Strength or Dexterity modifier (your choice), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest. You can also regain a use of Mounted Technique by expending a use of your Second Wind (no action required).

items: Feigned Shot. When you order your mount to take the Disengage action, as part of that action, you can use a Bonus action to make one extra Ranged attack with Advantage.

Braced Charge. When you order your mount to take the Dash action and hit a creature for the first time during that movement (minimum 10 feet) with a melee weapon that has the Reach property, the target takes extra damage equal to your Fighter level.
Pivot Shot. When you order your mount to take the Dodge action, you can use a Bonus action to make one extra Ranged attack that scores a Critical Hit on a roll of 18-20 on the d20.

Trample. When you order your mount to take the Dash action, you can move it through the space of one Large or smaller creature. It makes a Dexterity Saving Throw (DC 8 plus your mount's Strength modifier plus your Proficiency Bonus). Success: Your mount makes one melee attack against the creature. Failure: The creature has the {@condition Prone} condition and your mount makes one melee attack against the creature.

Sweeping Charge. When you order your mount to take the Dash action, you can deal damage equal to your Dexterity or Strength modifier to each creature that comes within range of your equipped melee weapon through the rest of your mount's movement. A creature can only take damage in this manner once per turn.

Swaying Seat. When you order your mount to take the Dodge action, you gain the benefits of Dodge as well. Until the start of your next turn, when a creature misses you with an attack, you may use a Reaction to make an attack against that creature with Advantage.

Parting Wind. When you order your mount to take the Disengage action, your mount ignores Difficult Terrain until the end of your turn and during this movement, when your mount leaves a creature's reach, if that creature is Medium sized or smaller, it has the {@condition Prone} condition.

entries: A metallic dragon that you have been bonded with using the spell {@spell Bond of the Dragonlords|OotDLREHH} can be used as your Tamed Steed for the abilities of this subclass.

entries.name: Master of the Reins
entries: You gain proficiency and Expertise in the Animal Handling skill. If you are already proficient, you gain proficiency in another Fighter skill of your choice.

entries.name: Subjugation
entries: When you reduce a Large sized Beast, or eligible Monstrosity or Dragon (see the Eligible Mounts table) to 0 Hit Points and choose to give it the {@condition Unconscious} condition instead of killing it, you can attempt to tame the creature during its forced Short Rest. To successfully tame the creature, it must have an Intelligence of 5 or lower, lack a Fly speed, and you must make a successful Wisdom (Animal Handling) check against the required DC. The DC is equal to 8 plus the creature's CR. On a success the creature becomes your Tamed Steed. On a failure, the creature becomes hostile and tries to escape. You cannot attempt to tame this creature again. At level 7 you can tame creatures with a Fly Speed, but only at the level shown on the Eligible Mounts table.

entries.name: Inherited Steed
entries: When you choose this subclass, you gain a loyal creature that is your Tamed Steed. Choose one of the following creatures: {@creature Giant Lizard}, {@creature Giant Seahorse}, or {@creature Warhorse}. If your GM allows, you can choose another Beast with a CR of ½ or lower that doesn't have a Fly Speed.

entries.name: You can have only one creature as your Tamed Steed at a time
entries: If you tame another creature, your previous Tamed Steed is no longer considered your Tamed Steed but remains Friendly toward you and you can stable it in a friendly settlement for 1 SP per day. Otherwise, the creature departs when it is able.

entries.name: Tamed Steed in Combat
entries: Your Tamed Steed is an ally to you and your allies. In combat, it shares your Initiative count, and it functions as a controlled mount while you ride it (as defined in the rules on mounted combat). If you have the {@condition Incapacitated} condition, the steed takes its turn immediately after yours and acts independently, focusing on protecting you.

entries.name: Restoring your Tamed Steed
entries: If your Tamed Steed has been reduced to 0 Hit Points, but not killed outright, you can cause it to instead have 1 Hit Point and the {@condition Unconscious} condition. After 1 minute, your Tamed Steed will recover to half of its Hit Points (rounded down) and no longer have the Unconscious condition. Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest unless you expend a use of your Second Wind to restore your use of it (no action required).

subclassFeature.name: Bonded Steed
entries: Every time you finish a Long Rest, your Tamed Steed gains Temporary Hit Points equal to your Fighter level.
When your mount takes damage, you can use your Reaction to take the damage instead.

subclassFeature.name: Knight's Reprisal
entries: When a creature hits your mount with an attack, you can use your Reaction to take the damage instead and make one attack against that creature.

subclassFeature.name: Knight of the Saddle
entries: When you are mounted and roll Initiative, you can add your Proficiency Bonus to the result and regain one use of your Mounted Technique if you're missing any uses of it.

subclassFeature.name: Mastery
entries: You know all mounted techniques. In addition, you regain all uses of Mounted Techniques when you finish a Short Rest.

subclassFeature.name: Hoplite
entries: The rank-and-file warriors of large cities are sometimes trained to fight in large armies of identically outfitted soldiers called hoplites. Hoplites fight behind heavy shields, which have notches to accommodate the use of spears and javelins. Additionally, they may carry a dagger called a xiphos for close quarters combat. Hoplites are famous for the use of the phalanx formation, which allows many soldiers to band together closely, benefiting from the protection of their neighbor's shield.

subclassFeature.name: Phalanx Fighting
entries: When you have a Shield equipped, you gain the following benefits:

items: You gain an additional +1 bonus to your AC.
You have Advantage on saving throws to avoid the {@condition Prone} condition or being pushed.
Any Ally standing within 5 feet of you has Half Cover.

entries: When you wield a spear, it gains the following properties:

items: It has the Reach property.
Damage increases to 1d8 (one-handed) or 1d10 (two-handed).

subclassFeature.name: Reprisal
entries: While you are wielding a weapon with the Reach property, whenever a creature within your reach makes an attack against an ally you can see, you can use your Reaction to make one melee attack against that creature.
If your attack hits, the target must subtract a number equal to your Proficiency Bonus from the triggering attack.

subclassFeature.name: Spear Mastery
entries: You gain the following benefits:

entries.name: Improved Reach
entries: When you wield a weapon with the Reach property, you add 10 feet to your reach instead of 5.

entries.name: Improved Critical
entries: Your attack rolls with javelins, or melee weapons with the Light or Reach property that also lack the Heavy property score a Critical Hit on a roll of 19 or 20 on the d20.

entries.name: Javelin Expert
entries: When you wield a javelin, its damage die becomes 1d8, and its range becomes 60/180 feet.

subclassFeature.name: Shield Mastery
entries: You gain the following benefits while you have a Shield equipped:

entries.name: Shield Rush
entries: When you use your Tactical Shift feature, you charge a creature with your Shield. The target must succeed on a Strength saving throw (DC 8 plus your Strength Modifier and Proficiency Bonus) or take {@damage 1d4} Bludgeoning damage, and you may give the target the {@condition Prone} condition, push it up to 10 feet, or both.

entries.name: Shield Wall
entries: When you are subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take half damage, you can use your Strength saving throw instead. You take no damage on a success and half damage on a failure. You may also choose one creature within 5 feet of you that is subjected to the same effect; they will take no damage if they succeed and only half damage if they fail.

subclassFeature.name: Promachos
entries: You are a champion of the front line, excelling in close combat and dueling.

entries.name: Superior Critical
entries: Your attack rolls with javelins, or melee weapons with the Light or Reach property that also lack the Heavy property score a Critical Hit on a roll of 19 or 20 on the d20. When you score a Critical Hit with a melee weapon, you deal additional damage equal to your Strength modifier. This extra damage is the same type as that dealt by the weapon. You knock away your target's Shield if they are wielding one. The Shield lands in a free space up to 10 feet away.

entries.name: Heroic Riposte
entries: When you are wielding a weapon in one hand and a creature misses you with a melee attack, you can take a Reaction to make one melee attack against it using a weapon with the Light property. You have Advantage on the attack roll, and you can both stow your one-handed weapon and draw this weapon as part of the same Reaction.

subclassFeature.name: Myrmidon Fury
entries: You have become a whirling machine of death in close quarters combat. When you take the Attack Action, you can forgo one of your attacks. When you do so, you may draw a melee weapon with the Light property as part of that forgoing, and then make one melee weapon attack with that Light weapon against each creature of your choice within 5 feet of you.
Make a separate attack roll for each target. You can use this feature once per turn.

subclassFeature.name: Warrior of the Shield
entries: Some monasteries teach a specialized form of combat that is very different from traditional monk fighting techniques. This style is known as the Way of the Shield, and it emphasizes the Shield as a living extension of the warrior. Monks of this tradition train to take Advantage of Shields and polearms, so that they can fight with or against large armies of hoplites in phalanx formations. Such monks commonly wear long red cloaks to disguise their intentions and add fluidity to their movements.

Temples that teach the Way of the Shield are often decorated with scrolls that exalt the feats of warriors who are fearless when faced with impossible odds. Massive armies may be surprised to encounter Resistance from a proud band of shield monks with less than a tenth of their numbers. Grandmasters of this tradition have even been known to stand alone against creatures many times their size.

subclassFeature.name: Aresian Technique
entries: You gain Training with Shields. Additionally, wielding a Shield does not impede your Acrobatic Movement, Martial Arts, Unarmored Movement, or Unarmored Defense features.
Your Shield is considered a monk weapon.
As long as you are wielding a Shield, Opportunity Attacks against you are made with Disadvantage.

subclassFeature.name: Shield Dancer
entries: You have learned new techniques for using Shields on the battlefield.

entries.name: Vaulting Strike
entries: As a Bonus Action on your turn, you may spend 1 Focus point to vault yourself into the air, leaping up to 15 feet in any direction. If you are wielding a Shield, then this leap does not provoke Opportunity Attacks. If you take the Attack action immediately after leaping, your melee attacks have Advantage and they score a Critical Hit on a roll of 18-20 on the d20 until the end of the current turn.

entries.name: Counterattack
entries: Whenever a creature makes an Opportunity Attack against you and misses, if you are using a Shield, you may use your Reaction to spin around and make a single melee weapon attack or Unarmed Strike against that creature, without interrupting your movement.

subclassFeature.name: Shell of the Dragon Turtle
