entries: You have learned to think of your Shield as an extension of your body. As a Reaction when you are attacked, you may spend 2 Focus points to gain an additional +5 AC from your Shield, including against the triggering attack, until the beginning of your next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Undaunted Spirit
entries: You can use your Shield as a ranged weapon. As an action, you can spend 1 Focus Point to throw your Shield at two targets within 90 feet. You may spend an additional 1 Focus Point to add an extra target. You may have up to four targets.

Make a ranged attack against each target. Being within 5 feet of a creature doesn't impose Disadvantage on the attack roll. On a hit, the target takes damage equal to two rolls of your Martial Arts dice, adding your Dexterity or Strength modifier. If your Shield is magical, any bonus to your AC is also added to damage.
Immediately after hitting or missing the last target, the Shield flies back to your hand.

subclassFeature.name: Oath of the Dragonlord
entries: Paladins who take the Oath of the Dragonlords are the last keepers of the traditions of the ancient order of the Dragonlords, from memorializing the oaths that bind great man and wondrous dragon to struggling for the mortals of Thylea in whatever ways they can. They dream to somehow, someway, discover a new dragon egg and raise the wyrmling within as an equal, to live destinies interlinked like the heroes of old.

items: Foster the soul bond between you and your dragon as equals.
Increase your wealth and knowledge by righteous means.
Aid your people and avenge them if you must.

entries.name: Using Oath of the Dragonlord Features
entries: Please note that some of your Oath of the Dragonlords features can be used on any dragon, while other features can only be used on a bonded dragon.

subclassFeature.name: Oath Spells
entries: The magic of your oath ensures you always have certain spells ready; when you reach a Paladin level specified in the Oath of the Dragonlords Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

entries.caption: Oath of the Dragonlord Spells
rows: {@spell Bond of the Dragonlords|OotDLREHH}, {@spell Feather Fall}
{@spell Dirge of the Dragonlords|OotDLREHH}, {@spell Warding Bond}

subclassFeature.name: Dragonlord Memory
entries: You know the Draconic language. In addition, you can cast the {@spell Bond of the Dragonlords|OotDLREHH} spell without Material Components if you are bonding yourself to a dragon. When you cast {@spell Dirge of the Dragonlords|OotDLREHH}, the cost for Material Components is half the required amount.

subclassFeature.name: Dragon's Resentment
entries: As a Magic action, you can expend one use of your Channel Divinity to mimic the repulsion breath of bronze dragons. Each creature of your choice within 15 feet of you must succeed on a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, they have the {@condition Prone} condition and their Speed is reduced to 0 until the end of their next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Dragon Sense
entries: When you use the Divine Sense option of your Channel Divinity, you also know the location of Dragons, including dragon eggs, within 1 mile of yourself. If you reach character level 5 without having found a dragon egg, your awareness opens further, and you automatically detect the dragon egg closest to you across any distance. In addition, you can communicate telepathically with your Bonded Dragon while it is within 60 feet of you with the Divine Sense option.
Once you discover a dragon egg, you can hatch it, then use the {@spell Bond of the Dragonlords|OotDLREHH} spell to bond with the hatchling that emerges.

subclassFeature.name: Mature Bond
entries: Your bonded dragon's initial growth spurt ends. It now uses the Juvenile stat block of the appropriate type.

entries.name: Mount
entries: As an alternative to the rules for controlling your dragon in the spell {@spell Bond of the Dragonlords|OotDLREHH}, you can use your bonded dragon as a Controlled Mount. You can also take a Bonus Action on your turn to command it to take an Action in its stat block or some other action instead of the actions limited to a Controlled Mount.

entries.name: Warded Mount
entries: When you cast the spell {@spell Warding Bond}, if your target is a dragon, then the casting time is a Bonus action. In addition, whenever a dragon starts their turn in your Aura of Protection, the dragon gains Temporary Hit Points equal to your Paladin level.

subclassFeature.name: Improved Bond
entries: Your connection with your bonded dragon continues to mature.

entries.name: Steady Mount
entries: Your bonded dragon loses its Unsteady Mount trait. When you command your bonded dragon to take the Bite action, the dragon can use it twice and add your Proficiency Bonus to the damage.

entries.name: Breath Master
entries: You can expend a use of your Channel Divinity to recharge one breath weapon of a Dragon within your Aura of Protection (no action required).

entries.name: Mental Bond
entries: When you communicate telepathically with your Bonded Dragon using Divine Sense it is now possible over any distance, though it can't extend to other planes of existence.

subclassFeature.name: Spiritual Bond
entries: As a Bonus Action, you forge a spiritual bond with a dragon you are mounted on. This bond lasts for 10 minutes and grants the following benefits.

entries.name: Draconic Weapon
entries: Your weapon attacks deal an extra {@dice 1d8} damage of the same type as the dragon's breath weapon.

entries.name: Divine Strikes
entries: The dragon can cast the {@spell Divine Smite} spell by expending your spell slots.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest. You can also restore your use of it by expending a level 5 spell slot (no action required).

subclassFeature.name: Amazon
entries: The Amazons are a warrior culture that emphasize the strength of the individual, in contrast to societies that defend themselves with large armies. A lone Amazonian huntress relies upon her mechanical companion, an avian stimfay, for support in battle. Every huntress learns to build and repair these mechanical birds when they are young, often forming deep and lasting bonds with the strange creatures. Each huntress is formidable in close quarters with her deadly kopis blade, but she also trains with an exotic ranged weapon called the chakram.

subclassFeature.name: Amazonian Magic
entries: Starting at level 3, you learn an additional spell when you reach certain levels in this class, as shown in the Amazonian Spells table.

subclassFeature.name: Stimfay Companion
entries: As an action, you can magically summon a {@creature Stimfay|OotDLREHH} that is bound to you. Stimfay are clockwork birds of prey that assist an Amazon with stalking her quarry. It appears in an unoccupied space of your choice within 30 feet of you. See its game statistics in the accompanying Stimfay stat block, which uses your proficiency bonus (PB) in several places.

The Stimfay is friendly to you and your companions. In combat, the Stimfay shares your initiative count, but it takes its turn immediately after yours. It can move and use its Reaction on its own, but unless you take a Bonus action on your turn to command it to take another action it will only take the Dodge action. That action can be one in its stat block or some other action. If you are Incapacitated, the Stimfay only takes the Dodge action.

The Stimfay remains until it is reduced to 0 Hit Points, until you use this feature to summon the Stimfay again, or until you die. Anything the Stimfay was wearing or carrying is left behind when the Stimfay vanishes.
Once you summon the Stimfay, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest, unless you expend a spell slot of level 1 or higher to summon it.

subclassFeature.name: Amazonian Battle Cry
entries: You gain the ability to enter the legendary frenzy of the Amazons by shouting your signature battle cry. At the start of your turn, you can shout your battle cry and enter a frenzy.
Your Frenzy lasts until the end of your next turn and grants you one of the following benefits:

items: You have Resistance to every damage type except Force, Necrotic, Psychic and Radiant.

You and your Stimfay have Advantage on attacks against a creature that you have Hunter's Mark on. When you or your Stimfay make an attack and deal damage to the target, you gain a bonus to the damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus.
Immediately after reducing a creature to 0 Hit Points using a melee or ranged weapon, you make an attack with the same weapon.

entries: You have Immunity to the {@condition Charmed} and {@condition Frightened} conditions while your Frenzy is active. If you're Charmed or Frightened when you enter your Frenzy, the condition ends on you.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (a minimum of once). You regain any expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

subclassFeature.name: Chakram Technique
entries: You've learned the famous Amazonian technique of ricocheting your Chakram to hit multiple targets. When you throw a Chakram, you can ignore all forms of Cover, and can target creatures that are not in your line of sight, such as around corners.

When you take the Attack action and hit a creature or object with a Ranged attack roll using a Chakram, you can forego your next attack this turn to target any number of additional creatures of your choice within 10 feet of that creature or object. Each creature makes a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC, taking the same amount of damage as your first target on a failure.

subclassFeature.name: Bracer Reflection
entries: You've learned to reflect attacks with your bracers. Whenever you would be hit by an attack, you may use your Reaction to shield yourself with your bracers. You gain a +5 bonus to AC against all attacks, including the attack that triggered this Reaction, until the beginning of your next turn. If the creature that made the triggering attack misses with that attack, it takes Force damage equal to a number of d6s equal to your Dexterity Modifier.
You may use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (a minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Short or Long Rest.

subclassFeature.name: Odyssean
entries: An Odyssean might look like a common soldier, carrying spears and shields like any hoplite, but the weapon they hone the most is their mind. While armies brutishly collide, these Rogues observe and find weaknesses to exploit, traveling far and away in search of the fame that comes with victory. Such harrowing journeys are what gives these soldiers their title, who then return home with the knowledge to turn any battlefield in the favor of their allies.

subclassFeature.name: Rogue of Many Ways
entries: You are rarely outwitted on the field of battle.

entries.name: Concealed Approach
entries: You can use an Action to stealthily guide your allies' movement. For the next 10 minutes, each creature of your choice within 30 feet of you has Advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks and leaves no tracks.

entries.name: Convincing
entries: Whenever you make an ability check using the Deception or Persuasion skills, you can make it as an Intelligence check even if it normally uses a different ability.

entries.name: Quick Scheme
entries: You can use a Bonus action to quickly devise a clever plan in the heat of battle. One creature within 60 feet of your choice that you can see must make an Intelligence saving throw. The DC equals 8 plus your Intelligence modifier and Proficiency Bonus. On a failed save, you and your allies have Advantage on attacks against that creature until the start of your next turn. This feature cannot be used on the same creature more than once per combat encounter.

subclassFeature.name: Vagrant Soldier
entries: You gain training with Medium Armor and Shields. In addition, Spears and Tridents have the Finesse property for you, and you can choose an additional weapon's mastery property when you use your Rogue Weapon Mastery feature.

subclassFeature.name: Notorious Trickster
entries: Your famed cleverness grants you the following benefits.

entries.name: Anxious Foes
entries: If you use a Cunning Strike option with a melee weapon attack, the target has Disadvantage on its saving throw against that Cunning Strike option.

entries.name: Vexing Assault
entries: When you attack using a weapon with the Finesse property and whose mastery property you can use, you can replace that property with the Vex property for that attack.

subclassFeature.name: Tenacious Survivor
entries: You've survived through enough ordeals through grim determination. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Quick Thinking
entries: You add your Intelligence modifier to Initiative rolls. When you roll Initiative, you may immediately move up to your Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks. In addition, you can exchange your Initiative roll result with a willing ally within 60 feet.

entries.name: Steel Resolve
entries: When you are forced to roll a saving throw, you can take a Reaction to gain Advantage on the triggering saving throw. Once you use this feature, you cannot do so again until you finish a Short Rest.

subclassFeature.name: Clever as the Gods
entries: You are constantly aware of opportunities and can even peek into the schemes of the gods. You are constantly under the effects of the {@spell Mind Blank} spell.
In addition, you gain the following Cunning Strike options.

items: Expose (Cost: 6d6). Each creature within 30 feet of the target can take a Reaction to make an attack against it.
Disrupt (Cost: 2d6). The target has Disadvantage on the saving throws it makes to maintain Concentration until the end of its next turn, including this attack.

subclassFeature.name: Divine Sorcery
entries: Your magic springs from the divine blood that flows through your veins. The gods have often been known to consort with mortals, and such unions sometimes produce half-divine offspring. These individuals are called demigods, and many of them are born with a powerful aptitude for magic.

Demigods exhibit powers that are related to the domain of their godly ancestor, but their magic is not constrained by this association. Rather, they may channel the power in their blood to improve the efficacy of any spell, regardless of its type. Additionally, the divine power that courses through their blood makes demigods impressive specimens of both physical fitness and beauty.

subclassFeature.name: Godly Ancestor
entries: Choose the Divine Domain of your godly ancestor from the Divine Sorcery and Spells table. Your godly ancestor was strongly associated with one of the core alignments: good, evil, law and chaos. You can cast each of the associated spells once without expending a spell slot and regain the ability to do so again when you finish a Short or Long Rest.

Additionally, whenever you make a Charisma ability check when interacting with Celestials (including gods), your Proficiency Bonus is doubled if it applies to the check, unless you have Expertise in the relevant skill.

entries.caption: Divine Sorcery and Spells
rows: {@spell Aid}, {@spell Bless}, {@spell Healing Word}, {@spell Lesser Restoration}
{@spell Ray of Sickness}, {@spell Witch Bolt}, {@spell Blindness/Deafness}, {@spell Heat Metal}
{@spell Command}, {@spell Guiding Bolt}, {@spell Augury}, {@spell Hold Person}
{@spell Charm Person}, {@spell Disguise Self}, {@spell Crown of Madness}, {@spell Hideous Laughter}

subclassFeature.name: Inherited Strength
entries: Your godly lineage bestows you with extraordinary strength and resilience. You are proficient in Strength saving throws. Additionally, you have Advantage on Constitution saving throws to retain Concentration on a spell.

subclassFeature.name: Empowered Magic
entries: Echoes of divine power flow through your spells. When you cast a spell, you may spend 1 Sorcery Point to increase the spell's effective level by 1. You cannot use this feature to increase a spell's effective level by more than 1. For example, if you use a level 5 spell slot to cast {@spell Fireball} as a level 5 spell, you may spend 1 Sorcery Point to cast the spell at level 6 instead.

subclassFeature.name: Divine Resistance
entries: Your divine blood allows you to shrug off effects that would destroy mere mortals. When you fail a saving throw, you can choose to succeed instead. If the triggering effect deals half damage on a success, you take no damage instead.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

subclassFeature.name: Ascendant Sorcery
entries: Your power has begun to rival your divine ancestor's. When you use the Empowered Magic feature, you may increase the spell's effective level by more than 1. You must spend 1 Sorcery Point for each effective level that you add to the spell. You may not increase the effective spell level above 10.

subclassFeature.name: The Fates Patron
entries: Your otherworldly patron is actually a trio of ancient beings: the coven of hags known as the Fates. The Fates weave the destinies of all gods and mortals in their magical loom, but whether they manipulate fate or merely record it is unknown. You have sworn yourself into the service of the Fates, and they sometimes reward you with glimpses into the future. However, you know that the Fates are utterly evil--whatever power that your pact affords you may pale in comparison to the ugly fate that they have likely prepared for you.

subclassFeature.name: Fates Spells
entries: The magic of the Fates ensures you always have certain spells ready; when you reach a Warlock level specified in the Fates Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

entries.caption: Fates Spells
rows: {@spell Detect Evil and Good}, {@spell Identify}, {@spell Levitate}, {@spell See Invisibility}

subclassFeature.name: Fate's Bidding
entries: At the end of a Short Rest or Long Rest, you can cast one Divination spell without expending a spell slot. The spell must be one that you know or have prepared, and you must provide any required material components.
When you cast a spell in this way, you gain Temporary Hit Points equal to your Warlock level.

subclassFeature.name: Threadreader's Insight
entries: When a creature that you can see within 60 feet casts a spell that requires a saving throw, you can take a Reaction to impose Disadvantage on one target of the spell's saving throw.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier and regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

subclassFeature.name: Fate's Foretelling
entries: You can call on the Fates to foretell future events. When you finish a Short or Long Rest, roll 1d20 and record the number you rolled. You can replace any d20 Test made by you or a creature that you can see with this roll. You must choose to do so before the roll. This foretelling roll can be used only once.

If you have no foretelling rolls, then as a Magic action, you may expend a Pact Magic spell slot to make a new foretelling roll. When you finish a Short or Long Rest, you lose any unused foretelling rolls.

subclassFeature.name: Fate's Demands
entries: The weight of your servitude grows heavy, and the burden only lessens when you help another creature meet its fate. The Fates reward your service by sharing their secrets with you.

entries.name: Sever the Thread
entries: When you reduce an Enemy to 0 Hit Points, you regain one expended Pact Magic spell slot, and you have the Fates Coven Spells prepared for 1 hour. Once you use this feature you cannot use it again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.
Fates Coven Spells: {@spell Bestow Curse}, {@spell Counterspell}, {@spell Identify}, {@spell Lightning Bolt}, {@spell Locate Object}, {@spell Polymorph}, {@spell Scrying}.

subclassFeature.name: Tangled Fate
entries: As a Magic Action, choose two creatures you can see within 60 feet. Each creature must make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC with Disadvantage. If both fail their saving throws, the creatures are Threadbound for 1 minute.
While Threadbound, when one creature takes damage, the other takes the same amount of damage. The damage it takes is Psychic damage.
If a Threadbound creature ends its turn more than 30 feet from the other, both creatures take {@damage 3d10} Psychic damage.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest, unless you expend a Pact Magic spell slot (no action required) to restore its use.

subclassFeature.name: Academy Philosopher
entries: Academy philosophers are great thinkers who do not specialize in any particular spell school, but rather spend their time analyzing the nature of reality and applying that learning to their magic. They usually spend many years studying at venerable schools where philosophers from many different disciplines gather. They enjoy participating in endless debates and dialogues, and they always seek to score points on those who champion rival schools of thought.

subclassFeature.name: Philosophical School
entries: When you become an academy philosopher, you choose from one of several philosophical schools to specialize in at your academy. This school becomes deeply ingrained in your way of thinking about the world.
Each Philosophy gives you a bonus to a Skill equal to your Intelligence Modifier.
In addition, you gain a feature that you can use a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

entries.name: Philosophy: Cynicism
entries: Cynics believe that one should reject material desires such as wealth and power. They advocate for an ascetic lifestyle, seeking to increase virtue by achieving harmony with nature.
Skill: Survival

Feature: As a Reaction when you finish casting a spell of level 1 or higher, you gain a number of Temporary Hit Points equal to twice the spell's level + your Intelligence modifier. You may instead grant these Temporary Hit Points to an ally you can see within 30 feet.

entries.name: Philosophy: Empiricism
entries: Empiricists believe that the world must be observed to be understood, and that the goal of philosophy is to understand why things are as they are.
Skill: Perception

Feature: At the start of your turn, you can closely observe a creature or object you can see within 60 feet. If the target is a creature, you learn its damage Vulnerabilities, Resistances and Immunities. In addition, you gain Advantage on your next attack roll against that target.

entries.name: Philosophy: Epicureanism
entries: Epicureans believe that the world is ruled by chance and that appealing to the gods is useless vanity. They believe that happiness is achieved by minimizing pain and living simple lives.
Skill: Medicine

Feature: When a creature you can see targets you with an attack, you can use your Reaction to impose Disadvantage on the attack roll. If the attack still hits, you gain Temporary Hit Points equal to twice your Intelligence modifier before the damage is dealt.

entries.name: Philosophy: Stoicism
entries: Stoics believe that we must develop self-control and fortitude in order to overcome our own self-destructive emotions. They advocate for humility and faith as antidotes to suffering.
Skill: Insight

Feature: When you are reduced to 0 Hit Points, but not killed outright, you can take a Reaction to expend a spell slot and drop to a number of Hit Points equal to four times the slot expended instead.

entries.name: Philosophy: Sophism
entries: Sophists specialize in developing rhetorical and aesthetic powers, and they advocate for principles of excellence and virtue in all endeavors.
Skill: Persuasion

Feature: As a Bonus action, you can create a dazzling rhetorical display. Choose one creature within 30 feet that can hear or see you. That creature must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC or suffer one of the following effects (your choice) until the end of your next turn:

items: It has Disadvantage on the next attack roll it makes.
It cannot take Reactions.
It cannot speak, cast a spell with a verbal component, or utter a command.

entries.name: Philosophy: Hedonism
entries: Hedonists believe that pleasure is the supreme good, and that everyone should seek to achieve the immediate gratification of their desires.
Skill: Performance
Feature: When you regain Hit Points from a spell or ability, you may choose to add twice your Wizard level to the number of Hit Points restored.

entries.name: Philosophy: Skepticism
entries: Skeptics believe that to truly possess knowledge of things is impossible. They believe that there are universal truths, but they cannot be understood well enough to shape dogmatic ideas about the world.
Skill: Arcana

Feature: When a creature you can see within 60 feet casts a spell, you can use your Reaction to sow magical doubt. The target must succeed on a Charisma saving throw against your spell save DC or the spell doesn't take effect until the start of the creature's next turn. If the caster dies or gains the {@condition Incapacitated} condition before that time, the spell fails.

subclassFeature.name: Mathematical Principles
entries: You have spent years solving complex mathematical equations, allowing you to shape your spells with precision. When you make a spell attack roll for a spell of 1st level or higher, you can treat a roll of 9 or lower on the d20 as a 10.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

subclassFeature.name: Metaphysical Principles
entries: When a creature casts a spell with a single target, you can take a Reaction to alter its course. If the spell is an effective level 5 or lower, you choose the target of the spell instead of the caster. If the spell is an effective level 6 or higher, the caster makes a Constitution saving throw and is subjected to the same effect on a failure.
Once you have used this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

subclassFeature.name: Magical Paradox
entries: You've spent years studying philosophical paradoxes, which allows you to work seemingly impossible feats with magic. Whenever you would lose Concentration on a spell for any reason, you may choose to maintain Concentration instead, as long as you are not Incapacitated. You may use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier, and you regain any expended uses after a Long Rest.

spell.name: Animal Polymorph
entries: This spell transforms a creature you can see within range into a new Beast form. The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or shape-shift into a Beast form for the duration. A shapechanger automatically succeeds on this saving throw.

The new form can be any Beast of CR 1 or less that does not have a Fly Speed. While in this new form, the target has the {@condition Charmed} condition until the spell ends. The target is Friendly to you, views you as trustworthy, and can understand simple commands such as "attack" or "stay" yet still acts as it chooses. If you or one of your allies damage the target, the spell ends.

The target gains a number of Temporary Hit Points equal to the Hit Points of the Beast form. These Temporary Hit Points vanish if any remain when the spell ends. The spell ends early on the target if it has no Temporary Hit Points left.
The target is limited in the actions it can perform by the anatomy of its new form, and it can't speak or cast spells.
The target's gear melds into the new form. The creature can't use or otherwise benefit from any of that equipment.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: If you use a level 5 or 6 spell slot, you can choose any Beast of CR 2 or less, and the Duration is Concentration, up to 1 hour. If you use a level 7 or higher spell slot, you can choose any Beast of CR 3 or less, and the Duration is 2 hours.

spell.name: Bond of the Dragonlords

components.m: an unhatched dragon egg, and magical armor, a shield, a weapon, a ring, a rod, a staff, or a wand worth at least 5,000 GP, which the spell consumes

entries: The verbal component of this spell is the Dragonlord Oath.

You permanently bond yourself or another humanoid creature of your choice to a newly-hatched dragon. A dragon that has been bonded can never be so again with another creature, and a humanoid that has been bonded can never be so again with another dragon.

entries.name: Dragon Growth
entries: Your bonded dragon starts with the Hatchling stat block of the appropriate type. A dragon grows into the appropriate Juvenile stat block after six months, and into the appropriate Young stat block after fifteen years.

entries.name: Controlling the Dragon
entries: Your bonded dragon is friendly to you and your companions, and it obeys your commands.

In combat, it shares your initiative count, but takes its turn immediately after yours. It can move and use its Reaction on its own, but the only action it takes on its turn is the Dodge action, unless you take a Bonus Action to command it to take another action. That action can be one in its stat block or some other action. If you have the {@condition Incapacitated} condition, your bonded dragon can take any action of its choice.

entries.name: Falling Unconscious
entries: If your bonded dragon reaches 0 Hit Points and doesn't die instantly, it follows the Falling Unconscious and Death Saving Throws rules.

spell.name: Dirge of the Dragonlords

components.m: an offering of gems and coins worth at least 1,000 GP, which the spell consumes

entries: You touch a bonded dragon that has been dead for no longer than 1 month and that died for any reason except old age. The dragon is revived with 1 Hit Point. This spell closes all wounds, neutralizes any poison affecting the creature when it died, and replaces damaged or missing organs and limbs.

spell.name: Fatebinding
entries: Choose two creatures that you can see. Both creatures must make Charisma saving throws, and they do so with Advantage if they are Hostile to you. If a creature is {@condition Charmed} by you, it has Disadvantage on this saving throw. If both creatures fail their saving throws, then their fates are now bound together.

items: Whenever one of the creatures takes damage, the other creature takes an identical amount of damage, unless both creatures took damage from the same single source, such as a {@spell Fireball} spell.

Whenever one of the creatures regains Hit Points, the other creature regains an identical number of Hit Points, unless both creatures regained Hit Points from the same single source, such as {@spell Mass Cure Wounds}.

entries: The two target creatures remain fate-bound for the duration of the spell, even if both targets are on different planes of existence.

spell.name: Seeds of Death

components.m: three or more minotaur teeth and alchemical fertilizer worth 100 GP

entries: You throw three minotaur teeth on to the ground in front of you. At the start of your next turn, three {@creature Minotaur Skeleton|OotDLREHH} erupt from the ground, fully formed. You can use a Bonus Action to shout commands at the minotaur skeletons if they are within 100 feet of you. Your commands must be general orders, such as "attack that enemy" or "guard this room." Once given an order, the minotaur skeletons will continue to follow it until the task is complete or until you issue another command. If the minotaur skeletons are given no commands, they will attack the nearest creature. When the spell ends, the minotaur skeletons dissolve into bone dust.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: You animate an extra minotaur skeleton for each spell slot level above 6.

spell.name: Sleeping Draught
entries: You open a draught and purple mist flows from you to a target creature. The creature makes a Wisdom saving throw. On a failure, it has the {@condition Unconscious} condition. On a success, the creature becomes drowsy; its Speed is halved, it can't take Reactions, and it makes one less melee or ranged attack until the end of its next turn.
The spell ends early if the target takes damage or if someone within 5 feet takes an Action to shake it out of the spell's effect.
A creature that does not sleep, or is immune to the {@condition Charmed} or {@condition Exhaustion} conditions, is not affected by this spell.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: This spell's range increases by 20 feet for each spell slot above 2.

spell.name: Sword of Fate
entries: Choose a creature that you can see. You curse the target for the duration of the spell, causing an illusionary sword to hang above the creature's head. Choose one of the following commands to shout out:

items: You cannot harm us. The target creature breaks this command if they target you or your allies with an attack or a spell that causes damage.
You cannot use magic. The target creature breaks this command if they cast a spell.
You cannot leave this area. The target creature breaks this command if it moves more than 30 feet from the spot it was standing when the spell was cast.

entries: If the creature acts contrary to your command, the sword becomes real, slices downward, and the creature makes a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, it takes {@damage 10d8} Slashing damage and one of its heads is removed if it is reduced to 0 Hit Points by this spell, instantly killing it if it can't survive without any heads. On a success, the creature takes half as much damage only.

spell.name: Theogenesis

components.m: offerings worth at least 10,000 GP, which are consumed, and all three Divine Artifacts: the Caduceus, the Ambrosia, and the Promethean Fire

entries: Theogenesis is a powerful spell that is used to place a divine spark into a mortal creature, unlocking the potential to ascend to godhood. The artifacts are not consumed when the spell is cast, but the offerings are. Choose a single target (non-divine) creature for the spell. You must remain in contact with the target for the duration of the casting. If contact is broken, both you and the target take {@damage 20d6} Radiant damage, and both the spell and the offering are wasted.

If the spell is successfully cast, then one of the greater gods must decide whether or not to grant the divine spark. The creature's relationship with the god determines its chance of success, and the base chance is 0%. Each of the bonuses below are cumulative:

items: The target shares at least one alignment axis with the greater god: +20%
The target has the exact same alignment as the greater god: +20%
The target has faithfully worshipped a god in the same pantheon for at least a year: +20%
The target has faithfully worshipped the greater god for at least a year: +30%

entries: Failure means that the greater god decides not to grant the divine spark. That greater god can't be chosen again if the spell is cast on the same target. Success means that the target has been permanently granted a divine spark. It can only be removed with a {@spell Wish} spell.

itemMastery.name: Return
entries: When this weapon is thrown, hit or miss, it returns to your hand. If the attack roll misses, the next attack roll you make has Advantage against that creature before the end of the current turn.

baseitem.name: Chakram
entries: This bladed circular disc is an unusual thrown weapon. Warriors who specialize in the chakram can learn to throw it in such a way that it returns to them after cutting the enemy.

baseitem.name: Dorata
entries: Dorata (singular dory) are spears carved from the wood of the ash tree.

baseitem.name: Honorblade
entries: A massive sword once forged for one-handed use by gygans. Now wielded with both hands by only the strongest humans, it delivers crushing blows due to its weighted tip.

baseitem.name: Kopis
entries: This forward-curving shortsword is heavier along the end of the blade. This gives it significantly more cutting power than a typical shortsword, allowing it to be used like an axe.
Note: the versatile two-handed form of this weapon deals Slashing damage, instead of Piercing damage.

baseitem.name: Makhaira
entries: This longsword has a single curved blade with a flat edge along the top.

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: Choose A or B: (A) {@item Calligrapher's Supplies|XPHB}, {@item Healer's Kit|XPHB}, {@item Fine Clothes|XPHB}, 14 GP; or (B) 50 GP

entries.name: For Players Who Love
entries: Cadmus, Atreus (Greek Tragedies)

entries.name: Restrictions
entries: None.

entries.name: Adventure Hook
entries: The Oracle reveals that she knows who can end the curse.

items: To end your family's curse.
To find the Gem of Brightness. This is a family heirloom, and only you can attune to it.

To find a greater family artifact that is key to ending the curse. Pick one magic item from this list: {@item Staff of Fire} (can be any melee weapon), {@item Belt of Fire Giant Strength} (this belt also grants resistance to fire), or an {@item Efreeti Bottle} (only you can take a Magic action to use it).

entries.name: Blessing of the Gods
entries: You and your direct family are immune to curses, diseases, and the {@condition Poisoned} condition.

You come from a great family or tribe that has been cursed for centuries, owing to the actions of one of your distant ancestors, who angered the Titans. Whatever the nature of your curse, the stigma has haunted you for all your life. Wherever you go, you are shunned by the ignorant and the superstitious. As a result, you have felt like an outsider for all your life. You know that as long as you remain cursed, you will be incapable of living a full life. Moreover, you are not sure that your family or your tribe will survive for another generation unless you find a way to lift the curse.

items.name: Tool Proficiency:
items.entry: Choose one kind of Musical Instrument

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: Choose A or B: (A) Musical Instrument (same as above), {@item Healer's Kit|XPHB}, {@item Quiver|XPHB}, {@item Traveler's Clothes|XPHB}, 14 GP; or (B) 50 GP

entries.name: For Players Who Love
entries: Heracles, Kratos

entries.name: Restrictions
entries: You must be a native to Thylea.

entries.name: Adventure Hook
entries: You have been summoned by the Oracle due to your fame and divine heritage.

entries.name: Heroic Tasks
entries: As a youth, the Oracle predicted a great destiny, one in which you might be able to join the pantheon alongside your divine father, who has recently fallen into despair and drunkenness. According to the Oracle, Pythor can be brought back from his drunken oblivion if you are able to achieve the three great labors that defeated him. You must find Pythor's last great love (your mother), defeat his greatest foe, and finish building his greatest weapon. Do these tasks, and your father will be redeemed.

items: Find your mother (Ophea, or a name created by you).
Defeat Pythor's greatest foe. According to legend this is a green dragon known as Hexia.
Finish building Pythor's greatest weapon. Choose either: a {@item Rod of Lordly Might} or a {@item Luck Blade} (can be any type of sword).

entries.name: Blessing of Health
entries: Your Constitution score increases by 2, up to a maximum of 22.
You are a mortal child of Pythor, the god of battle. Your temper is legendary. From an early age, you demonstrated unnatural talent in everything that interested you.

You've never met your father, but your mother was a woman famed for both her beauty and her skill as a harpist. She was carried away by a green dragon when you were very young. A family of soldiers adopted you, and then raised you to be a mighty champion for the city of Mytros. You are a favorite child of the city, and bards already sing of your great deeds while traveling the Heartlands.
The blood of Pythor burns in me. I'll find my mother and finish his weapon. Then gods themselves will make room at their table.

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: Choose A or B: (A) {@item Calligrapher's Supplies|XPHB}, {@item Fine Clothes|XPHB}, {@item Perfume|XPHB}, 8 GP; or (B) 50 GP

entries.name: For Players Who Love
entries: Achilles, Elric of Melniboné

entries.name: Restrictions
entries: Must be a native to Thylea.

entries.name: Adventure Hook
entries: The Oracle knows that your doom reflects the doom of the world. If you save yourself, you will be able to save the world.

items: To defeat the creature that has been fated to kill you.

To forge the one artifact that will protect you from your doom. These items provide resistance to all damage that originates from the creature that is fated to kill you. Choose one: {@item Robe of the Archmagi}, {@item Breastplate of Invulnerability}, or a {@item Cloak of Invisibility}.

entries.name: Blessing of Protection
entries: You gain a +1 bonus to your AC and to all saving throws.

You come from a famous and distinguished family with ancestors that include Dragonlords and gods. However, you had the misfortune of being born under a fell astrological sign, one that portended a doom of epic proportions. Your parents died shortly after you were born, under mysterious circumstances.

All your life you have been plagued by ill luck, and you have long suspected that your death will be as ugly as it is spectacular. The prophets and fortune tellers of Mytros make signs against evil when they see you in the street, and you have always been treated with prejudice and superstitious dread. Nevertheless, you've been called by fate to the Temple of the Oracle, and this can only mean that your nameless doom is now at hand. The Oracle has promised that your doom can be avoided, for she alone knows what will protect you.

items.name: Tool Proficiency:
items.entry: Choose one kind of Gaming Set

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: Choose A or B: (A) Gaming Set (same as above), {@item Fine Clothes|XPHB}, 29 GP; or (B) 50 GP

entries.name: For Players Who Love
entries: Perseus, Túrin Turambar

entries.name: Restrictions
entries: None.

entries.name: Adventure Hook
entries: The Oracle knows how to find the dragon that was responsible for your tragedy.

items: To kill the dragon responsible for your tragedy.

To find items that are key to killing dragons. Pick one lesser and one greater magic item from this list. Lesser: an {@item Armor of Resistance|DMG|Armor of Resistance (Fire)} (this can be any armor type) or a {@item Ring of Resistance|DMG|Ring of Resistance (Fire)} (only you can attune to this ring). Greater: a {@item Dragon Slayer|DMG} (can be any melee weapon) or a {@item Quiver of Ehlonna} (includes five Ammunition of Slaying, keyed to dragons), or a {@item Wand of Binding} (only you can attune).

entries.name: Blessing of Dragon Slaying
entries: You have Advantage on all attacks against creatures with the dragon type. Creatures with the dragon type have Disadvantage on saving throws against your spells.

You have a tragic past. Something terrible happened to you when you were young, and it forced you to reckon with the darkness within much sooner than anyone should ever have to. This tragic event shaped your identity and drove you to become who you are today. You know that it was a dragon who was responsible for destroying your childhood. The dragon might have razed your village to the ground--or it might have ruined your life in more insidious ways while polymorphed into the shape of a man or woman. Either way, you wish to discover the identity and the location of the dragon so that you can seek it out and exact brutal vengeance upon it.

items.name: Tool Proficiency:
items.entry: Choose one kind of Gaming Set

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: Choose A or B: (A) Gaming Set (same as above), {@item Traveler's Clothes|XPHB}, 29 GP; or (B) 50 GP

entries.name: For Players Who Love
entries: Jason and the Argonauts, Daenerys

entries.name: Restrictions
entries: Must be a native to Thylea.

entries.name: Adventure Hook
entries: The Oracle promises that the prophecy will put you on the path to become a Dragonlord.

items: To found a new order of Dragonlords. To do so you must find the Fortress of the Dragonlords. This fortress is the magic item {@item Instant Fortress}.
To attune with one of the Crowns of the Dragonlords. This will allow you to cast the spells {@spell Bond of the Dragonlords|OotDLREHH} and {@spell Dirge of the Dragonlords|OotDLREHH}.
To find a dragon egg, hatch it, and raise the dragon to be your companion.

entries.name: Blessing of the Dragonlords
entries: While mounted on a dragon, you gain that dragon's damage resistances, damage immunities and senses (Blindsight, Darkvision, and its passive Perception if it is greater than yours). If the dragon is an adult or ancient dragon, you can also use its Legendary Resistance (but this counts towards the total number of uses per day).

Ever since you were a child you've shown remarkable promise, effortlessly mastering every activity you've attempted. You have no explanation, but most people assume that you must have divine blood flowing through your veins. As you are from a common, or barbarian, family, you have been the target of seething envy from the children of the nobility and the wealthy who believe you do not deserve your gifts. You've therefore spent most of your life proving your worth. You want to achieve fame and fortune and have your name remembered down the ages. Mostly... you want to become a Dragonlord. If you could find a dragon egg and successfully hatch it, you could join the list of legendary heroes that are still remembered after five centuries. The call of the Oracle has given you an opportunity to prove your worth.

items.name: Tool Proficiency:
items.entry: Choose one kind of Musical Instrument

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: Choose A or B: (A) Musical Instrument (same as above), {@item Fine Clothes|XPHB}, 29 GP; or (B) 50 GP

entries.name: For Players Who Love
entries: Orpheus, Harry Potter

entries.name: Restrictions
entries: Must be a native to Thylea.

entries.name: Adventure Hook
entries: The Oracle claims that saving the world and fulfilling the prophecy will give you answers about your family's disappearance.

items: To be reunited with your family.

To reclaim your family name and legacy by tracking down your family artifacts. Pick one lesser and one greater family artifact from this list. Lesser: a {@item Ring of Protection} (worn by members of your lost family), an {@item Amulet of Health} (emblazoned with your family crest), or an {@item Ioun Stone, Awareness|DMG|Ioun Stone (Awareness)} (a jewel given to your ancestors by the gods). Greater: a {@item Helm of Brilliance} (worn by your ancestors, who were past rulers of Mytros), a {@item Dancing Sword} (can be of any type; contains the soul of the family's founder), or a {@item Rod of Absorption} (always carried by the leader of your family).

entries.name: Blessing of Magic Resistance
entries: You have Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

You were once in possession of the rarest treasure in Thylea: a truly happy life. You had a loving partner, beautiful children, and lived in a great house in the city of Mytros. As the first child of a powerful family with godly lineage, you were destined to be the next ruler of Mytros.

Then one day, everything changed. You returned home to find your house cold and empty. Your friends and neighbors have no memory of your family, almost as if they never existed. For a while, you struggled against insanity. Now you've resolved to find your family, whatever the cost. You'll travel to the ends of the earth and fight the gods themselves if needed. You'll do whatever it takes to bring back the people you love, even if everyone thinks you're crazy.

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: Choose A or B: (A) {@item Dagger|XPHB}, {@item Navigator's Tools|XPHB}, {@item Rope|XPHB}, {@item Traveler's Clothes|XPHB}, 20 GP; or (B) 50 GP

entries.name: For Players Who Love
entries: Narnia, Wizard of Oz

entries.name: Restrictions
entries: Must be an explorer from distant lands.

entries.name: Adventure Hook
entries: The Oracle thinks you have been sent from the outside world by the gods in order to fulfill the prophecy.

items: Find your surviving crew members.
Find a way to get back home.

Find the fabled treasures of the Dragonlords. The treasure trove includes three gems worth 10,000 GP (a diamond, a ruby, and a sapphire), 2,000 PP, and 10,000 GP. It also includes one of the following: a {@item Gem of Seeing}, a {@item Necklace of Prayer Beads}, {@item Glamoured Studded Leather}, or a {@item Rod of Rulership}.

entries.name: Blessing of Luck
entries: You may reroll any one attack roll, ability check, or saving throw. You must use the second roll. The blessing cannot be used again until after a long rest (at least several nights' sleep, as the GM decides).

You hail from a distant land, where your people worshiped foreign gods and spoke languages unknown to the people of Thylea. You sailed in search of the fabled treasures of the Dragonlords, but your ship and most of your crew were destroyed in a storm. Found by fishermen and brought to the city of Mytros, you discovered that your arrival had been prophesied by the Oracle.

You may not believe in any of the Oracle's prophecies, but one thing is for certain: you are somehow stranded on Thylea's shores, and your fate is now here. If the Oracle believes that you are one of the chosen few, then you must do what you can to help.

Perhaps one day our sacred order will be resurrected, but I cannot see it happening in my own lifetime. It would require courage, foresight, and leadership equal to that of Xander himself. Isadore might have done it, but she was taken from us too soon.

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: Choose A or B: (A) {@item Dagger|XPHB}, {@item Navigator's Tools|XPHB}, {@item Rope|XPHB}, {@item Thieves' Tools|XPHB}, {@item Fine Clothes|XPHB}, 20 GP; or (B) 50 GP

entries.name: For Players Who Love
entries: Odysseus, Captain America

entries.name: Restrictions
entries: Must be an explorer from distant lands.

entries.name: Adventure Hook
entries: You are the Oracle's favorite pet.

items: To find if you have any descendants.

To reclaim your title as a Dragonlord. Crown: Attune with one of the Crowns of the Dragonlords. This will allow you to cast the spells {@spell Bond of the Dragonlords|OotDLREHH} and {@spell Dirge of the Dragonlords|OotDLREHH}. Dragon: Find a dragon egg, hatch it, and raise the dragon to be your companion.

To get back your fabled armor. Choose one item from the following list: {@item Boots of Speed} (emblazoned with the image of your old dragon mount), {@item Dragon Scale Mail} (made from the scales, given willingly, of your old dragon mount), or a {@item Cloak of the Bat} (only you can attune to this cloak; instead of transforming into a bat, this cloak allows you to transform into a pseudodragon).

entries.name: Blessing of the Dragonlords
entries: While mounted on a dragon, you gain that dragon's damage resistances, damage immunities and senses (Blindsight, Darkvision, and its passive Perception if it is greater than yours). If the dragon is an adult or ancient dragon, you can also use its Legendary Resistance (but this counts towards the total number of uses per day).

You are one of the Dragonlords, the legendary outside explorers who first discovered Thylea. You were present when the tiny settlement of Mytros was founded, but you've been missing for almost 500 years. During an expedition into the Cerulean Gulf, you fell victim to the irresistible charms of a nymph named Versi. You've spent the last five centuries in a waking dream, trapped in her cave with no knowledge of time passing or events on the mainland. Versi released her hold on you when you were called by fate to save Thylea, but she made you swear an oath to return to her once your quest is completed. Versi is known as the Oracle by most of the inhabitants of Thylea.
The time that you have spent with Versi has created gaps in your memory. You are no longer the great Dragonlord that you once were. You must relearn all of the skills lost to you.

race.name: Grim

sizeEntry.name: Size:
entries: Medium or Small, chosen when you select this species.

The grims are children of Grimnir. Most are comfortable beneath murky lake waters in forests that no raider has ever found. Others were forced to flee their refuges, pushed out by raiders and monsters. The grim often form small communities that linger near, but not entirely within, existing raider towns.

All grims long for water--whether sea, river, or pool. Grims breathe underwater through a primal magic that no mortal truly understands. Their ears are wide and pointed, and they tend to have green or blue skin to blend in with their murky habitats.

entries.name: Primal Drive
entries: Your Primal instincts shape your physical adaptations. Choose one of the following Primal Drives from the Primal Drive table: Musician or Lurker. You gain the level 1 benefit of that drive. You can change your choice whenever you gain a character level. If a feature level grants a spell, you always have that spell prepared. You can cast it once without a spell slot or needing a material component, and you regain the ability to cast it in that way when you finish a Long Rest. You can also cast the spell using any spell slots you have of the appropriate level. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for the spells you cast with this trait (choose the ability when you select the drive).

entries.caption: Primal Drive
rows: Share the Music. As a Magic action, you grant one willing creature proficiency with a Musical Instrument of your choice for up to one hour. Amphibious. You can breathe underwater and can take a Magic action to grant one willing creature this benefit for up to one hour. Sweet Voice. You have proficiency in the Performance skill.
You always have the {@spell Sleep} spell prepared.
You always have the {@spell Suggestion} spell prepared.

Inflict Harm. Once per turn when you hit an opponent with a weapon or Unarmed Strike, you can inflict Cold damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus. Ambusher. Your Long Jump and High Jump distances are doubled (after standard calculation).
You always have the {@spell Fog Cloud} spell prepared.
You always have the {@spell Invisibility} spell prepared.

entries: You can gain a Climb Speed or Swim Speed equal to your Speed while you have the Lurker or Musician drive active, respectively, at your GM's discretion.

Grims have conflicted souls. They originated with Grimnir when it was created and perhaps their internal conflict arises from the turmoil that surrounded that creation. Some grims live their entire lives indulging in their music--performing or teaching others how to play instruments, sing, and entertain. Others resent the encroachment of mortals into their pools and waterfalls and do what they can to deter trespassers.

entries.name: Grim Names
entries: Their names tend to be that of the community of which they are a part, though they prefer short names, often with only a single syllable.
Names: Ack, Cay, Clu, Fas, Gorm, Hil, Liv, Nok, Ru, Strom, Tora, Toke, Ulf.

race.name: Tallfolk
entries: Since the Exodus, tales of enormous men and women appearing in the forests of Turnfjall have spread. Over time a community of these large humanoids have formed a clan of their own--the Risa. Most tallfolk come close to (or slightly exceed) 10 feet in height, and they weigh several hundred pounds.

entries.name: Bulky
entries: Your larger size allows you to double the range of any thrown weapon. Additionally, when you make a melee attack, your reach is increased by 5 feet.

entries.name: Breaking Point
entries: While Bloodied, on your turn, you can grant yourself Advantage on your next Attack roll (no action required) and deal +2 extra damage if it hits. You can do this a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus and regain all expended uses on a Long Rest.

entries.name: Giant Ancestry
entries: Pick one of the following subraces: Earth-Child or Cold-Child. This subrace grants additional special traits.

Many tallfolk, as they age, begin to hear whispers... a faceless voice whose words are never heard clearly. Yet the meaning is inescapable: the voice urges them towards violence and anger, and often towards the mountains of Turnfjall. And so, they counter-balance that with a gentleness that belies their great size. But those that anger the tallfolk always reap consequences.

entries.name: Tallfolk Names
entries: Names: Artog, Blar, Dwat, Haw, Mon, Nock, Britta, Rima, Rowl, Spar, Stroth.
The Tallfolk are what happens when witches steal giant babies and raise them wrong.

race.name: Wicker

sizeEntry.name: Size:
entries: Medium or Small, chosen when you select this species.

Woven together when the world was created, the wicker are unusual constructs. Though made from wood they are clearly separate and apart from the natural world. They were built for a purpose, but that purpose has long been forgotten.

entries.name: A Creator's Soul
entries: You gain proficiency in two Tools of your choice.

entries.name: Neither Alive nor Dead
entries: You have several advantages over other creatures.

items: You don't gain Exhaustion levels from dehydration, malnutrition, or suffocation.
You can't unwillingly have your form altered by a spell or effect.

entries.name: Aversion to Fire
entries: You have Disadvantage on saving throws against effects that include Fire damage.

entries.name: Build
entries: Choose one of the following benefits: Builder or Watcher.

entries.name: Builder
entries: During a Long Rest a builder wicker can add and remove limbs. When you finish a Long Rest, choose one of the following:

items: Two Additional Legs. Increase your Speed by 10 feet.
Tool Arm. You gain proficiency in two Artisan's Tools of your choice and this arm acts as a set of each of the chosen tools.
Shield Arm. This arm acts as a donned Shield, for which you have Training. If you have a Shield in one of your main hands, you choose which Shield you benefit from.

Spiked Arm. This arm acts as a Simple weapon with which you have proficiency. On a hit, the target takes 1d6 Piercing damage plus your Strength modifier, and if that creature uses the Dash, Disengage, or Dodge action before the end of your next turn, it also takes Piercing damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus.

Hidden. You can magically appear as a Humanoid species of your choice in size equal to yours, and you can change your choice when you finish a Long Rest. A suspicious creature can make a DC 18 Intelligence (Investigation) check to discover your true creature type. If sensed by {@spell Detect Magic}, you give off a magical aura, but not a school of magic.
Watchful. You gain proficiency in either the Persuasion or Insight skill.

Change is Inevitable. The watcher can tear off their facade and become a builder. This transformation takes one minute and is irrevocable. The wicker loses their watcher features and gains the builder features.

entries: The wicker seek their own identity. Some have attempted to band together into communities of their own, while others travel the world with no knowledge that others like them exist. Most wicker have a drive to build--whether it be jewelry, weapons, or buildings.

entries.name: Wicker Names
entries: A wicker tends to be named by those around it, perhaps for the forest where it is found or how it acted when first talked to.
Names: Agar, Bark, Booton, Brough, Cowick, Fand, Fothat, Glion, Growl, Halbrook, Isen, Kin, Lowen, Rivest, Roth, Tol, Vin.
These twiggy little shits run around building houses like it'll give them a soul. Pathetic. I've seen fence posts with more personality and better wood.

race.name: Automatos
entries: Unlike other constructs shaped only to obey, the automatos possesses the freedom to choose its own path. It speaks with understanding and feels with intention.

entries.name: Forged Endurance
entries: You have Advantage on saving throws to avoid or end the {@condition Poisoned} condition. You have Resistance to Poison damage.

entries.name: Construct
entries: You don't need to eat, drink, or breathe.

entries.name: Tarnished Truth
entries: When you knowingly speak a lie, your metal shell visibly darkens. Each lie increases the tarnish by one stage, to a maximum of five stages. At five stages, your shell is soot-black. The tarnish fades after a Long Rest.

entries.name: Mechanical Features
entries: After finishing a Long Rest, you can choose a feature below. You retain this feature until you complete another Long Rest. At Level 3 you can choose two features instead of one. At Level 5 you can choose three features.

items: Chameleon Shell: You have Advantage on Dexterity checks to Hide. When you take the Hide action, you can take on the coloration of your surroundings. If you do, the Invisible condition will not end as a result of a creature having line of sight to you, and you can't be perceived by Truesight while you have the Hide action's Invisible condition. You lose this benefit if you move 5+ feet, and your Speed is 0 until the end of the current turn when you use this trait.
Conduction: When you take Lightning damage, your next melee attack deals an extra {@damage 3d6} Lightning damage to the target and every creature of your choice within 5 feet of it.
Enhanced Memory: You have Advantage on Intelligence ability checks and saving throws. You may use the Study Action as a Bonus Action.
Gyroscopic Balance: You are Immune to the {@condition Prone} condition, and your movement is not reduced in Difficult Terrain.
Heat Sinks: You have Resistance to Fire damage. When you take Fire damage you also have Resistance to Cold damage until the end of your next turn.
Magnetic Grips: You have a Climb Speed equal to your Speed.
Night Vision: You have Darkvision out to 60 feet.
Telescopic Optics: You may use the Search Action as a Bonus Action to make a Wisdom (Perception) check to spot something.

entries: Born from Volkan's lonely genius, the automatos was crafted as a companion worthy of thought. To grant it a soul, Volkan carved away a fragment of his own and bound it to a bronze body. He has forged many wonders, but he has only ever made one automatos, and in private he calls it his child. If your GM allows it, your origin may differ--a titan or master artificer may have forged you instead.

The automatos differs from all other constructs in a profound way: it bears a true mortal soul. For the automatos to possess free will, it must also possess mortality. Though blessed with a soul, the automatos is still a body of metal and magic. Its bronze frame is strong and tireless, untouched by poison or disease, yet it suffers dents, cracks, and the slow decay of age. Unlike lesser constructs, it can mend and even modify itself.

Volkan feared that his one creation might someday stray into cruelty, so he forged subtle safeguards into its body. These do not deny the automatos its freedom, but they burden every misdeed with consequence.

entries.name: Names and Personality
entries: The automatos chooses its own name, inspired by the first word or idea it encountered upon awakening. It might select a name tied to virtue, such as Harmony or Valor, or take the name of a mortal it admired.

race.name: Gygan

sizeEntry.name: Size:
entries: Medium; while small for one of your kind, you still tower over most others (7-8 feet tall, over 400 pounds).

Gygans are a race of six-armed, one-eyed giants shaped to embody strength and unity by the Titan, Sydon. Their ancestors built grand city-states where athletic games honored the gods as much as war did.

entries.name: Six Arms
entries: You have six arms and hands, which can be used for the Two-Handed property, Versatile property, and a free hand for casting a spell with a Somatic component. In addition, you can use three hands to wield a weapon with the Heavy property to ignore its Strength or Dexterity requirements. For example, you can hold a Shield in one hand, a Greatsword in three, and two daggers in one hand each.
For every two free hands you have, you can do one of the following on your turn:

items: Take the Help action as a Bonus Action.
Make an Unarmed Strike as a Bonus Action. You must use the Grapple option.
Fire an additional piece of ammunition when using a weapon with the Loading property.
Interact with an additional object.

entries: You are still bound to other restrictions that apply to a character. Examples include:

items: You can't have more than one Shield equipped.
You can't make the extra attack from a weapon with the Light property or Nick mastery without making an attack using a Light weapon first.

entries.name: Poor Depth Perception
entries: You have Disadvantage on ranged attack rolls made against targets more than 30 feet away.

entries.name: Towering Might
entries: You have Advantage on any ability check you make to end the {@condition Grappled} condition. You also count as one size larger when determining your carrying capacity.

Today's gygans still carry echoes of their golden age. They build stone villas and vineyards on lonely hillsides, crafting their own art and music. Their six arms grant them extraordinary balance and strength, and many channel this gift into martial arts, performance, or labor that celebrates precision and endurance.

Among gygans, strength is both virtue and necessity. From birth, every child is judged by the elders of the family estate for signs of vigor and divine favor. Those born too small or malformed are cast out, left to die, exposed to the elements. Yet fate sometimes spares the forsaken. A few of these abandoned children are discovered by farmers or shepherds who raise them in secret, far from gygan estates.

entries.name: Gygan Names
entries: Gygan names are short, resonant, and powerful; echoes of their ancient Giantish tongue. Family or clan names often honor natural forces or sacred places that shaped their lineage.
Names: Brak, Vura, Torgan, Ilyra, Dhom, Kaelra, Surnak.
Family Names: Thunderous Echo, of Stonewatch, of the Howling Winds, of Stony Point.

race.name: Jancan Cyclops

sizeEntry.name: Size:
entries: Medium; while small for one of your kind, you still tower over most others (7-8 feet tall, over 400 pounds).

Among the cyclopes, a rare child is sometimes born with ten fingers on each hand and ten toes on each foot. These extraordinary beings are known as jancan. Where ordinary cyclopes struggle to recall their lost heritage, the jancan embody fragments of it.

entries.name: Forge Toughened Body
entries: You have Resistance to Fire damage.

entries.name: Master Craftsman
entries: You gain proficiency in Smith's Tools and Mason's Tools. If you already have proficiency, you may choose a different tools proficiency.

Raw materials cost half as much for you to craft any nonmagical item. When determining crafting time, you count as two characters working at once. You may still have one assistant who counts as an additional character for this purpose.

entries.name: Many Fingered Agility
entries: You have Advantage on Dexterity checks when using Sleight of Hand, Thieves' Tools, or using Performance to play a musical instrument.

entries.name: Many Fingered Strength
entries: Your grip is incredibly strong. While you are grappling a creature, that creature takes Bludgeoning damage equal to your Strength modifier at the start of each of its turns.

entries.name: Poor Depth Perception
entries: You have Disadvantage on ranged attack rolls made against targets more than 30 feet away.

entries.name: Towering Might
entries: You have Advantage on any ability check you make to end the {@condition Grappled} condition. You also count as one size larger when determining your carrying capacity.

Jancan are revered because of their unparalleled skill as smiths. Their many-fingered hands can shape metal with a precision no other giant can match. Each creation is bound to the soul of a single owner, shining with power only while that owner lives. When the wielder dies, the enchantment fades, leaving behind only the memory of a masterwork forged by a jancan's gifted hands.

The cyclopes used to have a greater purpose--to forge weapons to be used by the gods; to guard great treasure vaults filled with doomsday weapons; or to build massive fortresses, towers, and other wondrous architecture. These great tasks have long since been abandoned or forgotten.
Give a jancan iron and time, and it will sing. Their many fingers feel flaws no other smith can sense, and correct them before the hammer falls.

entries.name: Jancan Names
entries: Jancan names often differ from the coarse, guttural names of ordinary cyclopes. Their names tend to be heavier, deliberate, and shaped by the cadence of hammer on anvil. Unlike their kin, jancan frequently adopt titles rather than clan names, reflecting their craft or the forge that shaped them.
Names: Korvak, Thalren, Jornaka, Velmuk, Rithena, Mograk, Yandrel.

race.name: Myrmekes
entries: The myrmekes are an insectoid race that resemble humanoid ants with glossy black carapaces and shimmering, multicolored wings. The defining trait of every myrmekes is the shared consciousness that binds them.

entries.name: Chitin Armor
entries: Your glossy carapace protects you. When you aren't wearing armor, your AC equals 13 plus your Dexterity modifier.

entries.name: Iridescent Wings
entries: Your wings allow bursts of movement. You can jump up to 20 feet by spending 10 feet of movement. You can use this trait once per turn. When you reach character level 5, your wings grow strong and coordinated. You have a Fly Speed equal to your Speed.

entries.name: Perfect Imitation
entries: You can learn the following abilities from other creatures. Once you've learned one of them, you can't learn a new ability of the same type until you finish a Long Rest. These abilities last until you learn a new ability of the same type.

items: Skill: When a creature you can see makes an ability check using a skill they are proficient in, you can gain proficiency in that skill.
Combat: When a creature you can see makes a weapon attack with a weapon they are proficient in, you can gain proficiency with that weapon.
Magic: When a creature you can see casts a cantrip, you can learn that cantrip. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for it.
Speech: When a creature you can hear speaks a language for at least 1 minute, you can learn that language.

entries.name: Residual Hive Mind
entries: You can telepathically communicate with any creature within 30 feet that understands at least one language. Once per long rest, you may form a Minor Hive with up to a number of willing creatures equal to your Proficiency Modifier for 1 hour. While linked:

items: Each member within 30 feet has Advantage on Insight checks.
Members may communicate telepathically, while within 30 feet of each other.

entries: Sometimes a myrmekes becomes severed from the hive mind, cast adrift in a world suddenly stripped of voices and purpose. Most do not survive this terrifying isolation, yet on the rarest of occasions, a lone myrmekes endures.

Imitation is the greatest strength of the myrmekes, and also their greatest weakness. They are not creative in the way other humanoid species are, but their ability to observe and replicate borders on supernatural.

entries.name: Myrmekes Names
entries: Myrmekes do not receive names from a hive, for the swarm has no need for individual identity. A lone myrmekes chooses a name only after separation, often inspired by the first sensation or creature it encounters in its new life.
Names: Kritt, Zarra, Vek, Nali, Chyrr, Omos, Tikkar.

race.name: Nymph
entries: Nymphs are fey spirits that manifest from the beauty of the elemental forces of creation. There are many kinds of nymphs--dryads of the forests, naiads of the rivers, oreads of the mountains, aurae of the night sky, and nereids of the sea.

entries.name: Fey Ancestry
entries: You have Advantage on saving throws you make to avoid or end the {@condition Charmed} condition.

entries.name: Enthralling Beauty
entries: You possess unearthly grace and beauty, which allows you to dazzle and charm those who are susceptible to such things. You have Proficiency in the Persuasion skill. Additionally, you can cast the {@spell Charm Person} spell once with this trait and regain the ability to do so when you finish a short or long rest. Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this spell.

entries.name: Nymph Ancestry
entries: When you create your nymph, choose one of the following ancestries: Night, Woodlands, Rivers, Oceans, or Mountains. You gain the level 1 benefit of that ancestry. When you reach character levels 3 and 7, you learn a higher-level spell, as shown on the table. You always have that spell prepared. You can cast it once without a spell slot, and you regain the ability to cast it in that way when you finish a Long Rest. You can also cast the spell using any spell slots you have of the appropriate level. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for the spells you cast with this trait (choose the ability when you select the ancestry).

entries.caption: Nymph Ancestries
rows: You have Darkvision with a range of 120 feet.
You have a Swim Speed of 40 feet. You can hold your breath for 1 hour.
You have a Swim Speed of 40 feet. You can breathe air and water.
You have Darkvision with a range of 60 feet.

entries: They have walked the earth for millennia, ever since the Great Mother awakened them from the trees, waters, rocks, and breezes. Nymphs are most at home in nature, but they have been known to disguise themselves and live amongst mortals, for they are desperately curious about the civilized world.

Nymphs are famed for their feminine charms, but they are not exclusively female. Some are awakened from the elements with a mix of masculine and feminine features, and others are quintessential specimens of male splendor.

entries.name: Nymph Names
entries: Nymphs have names that sound beautiful and elemental.
Male Names: Celano, Elion, Eratheis, Hyllis, Limnade, Linos, Myrmex, Olbia, Pega, Potameid, Pyron, Taygete.
Female Names: Aegle, Alcyone, Arethusa, Asterope, Brettia, Brisa, Calybe, Crinae, Crimisa, Dodone, Electra, Erythia, Hesperia, Himalia, Oeneis, Laodice, Maia, Merope, Polydora, Rhene, Semestra.

race.name: Nyxian
entries: The Nyxian are mortals touched by the primordial goddess of night, born with talents and instincts tied to ancient principles such as dreams, fate, fear, and mortality. Though mortal in body, their spirits carry echoes of the darkness beyond creation.

entries.name: Born of the Night
entries: You have Darkvision out to 60 feet.

entries.name: Night Touched
entries: Your presence unsettles higher beings. You have Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects caused by creatures of the Celestial and Fiend creature types and by creatures with the Titan tag.

entries.name: Living Concept
entries: Choose a Cosmic Principle from the table below. You radiate an aura in a 10-foot Emanation. You and your Allies within the aura gain the level 1 benefits of that principle. If another Nyxian is present, a creature can only be subjected to the effects of one Living Concept's aura at a time, its choice.

entries.caption: Cosmic Principles
rows: You have Resistance to Psychic damage. You have Advantage on saving throws to avoid or end the {@condition Charmed} condition.
The target can't speak a deliberate lie and takes {@damage 2d6} Psychic damage.
Whenever you make a saving throw, you add {@dice 1d4} to the roll.
Whenever the target makes an attack roll or saving throw, they must subtract {@dice 1d4} from the attack roll or save.
You have Advantage on saving throws to avoid or end the {@condition Frightened} condition.
The target gains the {@condition Frightened} condition.
You have Advantage on Insight and Persuasion checks.
The target has the {@condition Charmed} condition.
You have Advantage on Death Saving Throws. You gain {@dice 1d4} Temporary Hit Points at the start of each of your turns.
Whenever you make an attack roll, you add {@dice 1d4} to the roll.
You have Advantage on Charisma saving throws.
The target has the {@condition Charmed} condition.
You have Resistance to Necrotic and Poison damage.
The target has the {@condition Blinded} and {@condition Deafened} conditions.

entries.name: Discord
entries: Beginning at character level 5, you can take a Bonus Action to turn your Living Concept aura against your enemies for 1 minute or until you have the {@condition Incapacitated} condition. Whenever the Emanation enters an Enemy's space and whenever an Enemy enters the Emanation or ends its turn there, the creature makes a Wisdom saving throw (DC 8 plus your Proficiency Bonus and Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma modifier; choose the ability when you select this species). On a failed save, it suffers the level 5 effects from your chosen Cosmic Principle until the end of its next turn. A creature makes this save only once a turn.

You can use this trait a number of times equal to half your Proficiency Bonus and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest. If another Nyxian is present, a creature can only be subjected to the effects of one Living Concept's aura at a time, its choice.

Often referred to as the Dreamer, Nyx is the unknowable force from which dreams and possibility first emerged. She rests beyond the outermost stars, yet her influence lingers in the Nether Sea, an underworld ocean formed from the raw primordial substance she shaped in ages before the world existed.

Nyx does not choose her offspring as other gods do. Instead, her essence surfaces unpredictably within certain bloodlines, manifesting when the veil between the mortal and the primordial grows thin. Despite their origins, Nyxian are entirely mortal; they age, bleed, and die as all mortals do.
A mortal who kills a Nyxian suffers no more ill fortune than fate already promised. But when a god or titan slays one of these children, catastrophe inevitably follows.

entries.name: Nyxian Names
entries: A Nyxian's name evokes ancient forces and primordial concepts. Parents of a Nyxian always seem to know the child's name instinctually, as if whispered by the cosmic principle that dwells within them.
Male: Algos, Erebus, Geras, Hypnos, Icelus, Moros, Oneiros, Phobetor, Thanatos.
Female: Achlys, Arethusa, Atropos, Chrysothemis, Clotho, Eris, Erytheia, Hesperia, Hespere, Lachesis, Lipara, Nemesis, Oizys, Poine.

race.name: Thylean Centaur

sizeEntry.name: Size:
entries: Medium, but you tower over most other species (6'6"-7 feet tall, weighing 700-900 pounds).

A noble species that roams the great plains of the world, centaurs are both feared and respected by other intelligent creatures. Centaur legends claim that they are the offspring of a powerful god of war that came down to the mortal plane in the form of a stallion.

entries.name: Charge
entries: If you move at least 15 feet in a straight line towards a target immediately before hitting it with a melee attack, you can add a bonus {@dice 1d6} damage to the attack's damage roll. You can use this trait once on each of your turns.

entries.name: Gallop
entries: Opportunity Attacks have Disadvantage against you.

entries.name: Mountable
entries: You count as one size larger when determining if you can be mounted.

entries.name: Quadrapedal Stride
entries: Climbing or maneuvering in tight spaces is considered Difficult Terrain for you.

entries.name: Large Body
