entries: You also count as one size larger when determining your carrying capacity.

Centaurs possess a humanoid torso with a horse's lower body. They are as varied in coloration and physical build as humans and horses. Centaurs are a proud people. They view themselves as superior to all other species and demand respect and adulation.

Centaurs are a tribal people, fiercely loyal to members of their tribe, and will never leave one of their own behind. If they join an adventuring group, they will often consider that group to be their current tribe.

Centaurs are distrustful of the civilized species of Thylea. In the First War that raged five centuries ago, thousands of centaurs were killed by the invading Dragonlords, and the centaurs have never forgotten or forgiven.

I once saw a stampede of centaurs going to battle against the cyclopes, west of Xanderia. There is no more marvelous sight in Thylea than their spears gleaming in the sun of the steppes, wild manes flowing, hooves thundering. That night, they feasted and sang under the stars, calling out to me from afar, but I confess that I was too afraid to draw near.

entries.name: Centaur Names
entries: Male Names: Agrius (Agri), Amycus (Amy), Asbolus (Az), Bienor, Chiron, Cyllarus (Cyl), Dictys, Eurytus (Tus), Elatus, Eurytion (Yuri), Hylaeus (Hyla), Nessus, Perimedes (Peri), Pholus, Rhoetus (Rote), Thaumas (Tom).
Female Names: Agaria, Biano, Cylla, Diena, Eura, Hylonome (Hylo), Heranae (Hera), Nessicana (Nessie), Nara, Ponadata (Pona), Rhaelatisis (Rala), Rhaena (Rain), Seranu (Sara).

race.name: Thylean Medusa
entries: Medusa are humanoids that have made a bargain with dark powers to achieve beauty, eternal youth, great wealth, or some other mortal desire. As a consequence, their hair has been replaced with snakes, and their eyes have the power to petrify the unwary.

entries.name: Darkvision
entries: Your eyes are adapted to dark places, giving you Darkvision out to 120 feet.

entries.name: Snake Hair
entries: You can attack with your snake hair. This is a melee weapon attack with an attack bonus equal to your Proficiency Bonus + your Dexterity modifier. It does {@damage 1d6} Piercing damage on a hit and the target makes a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 plus your Constitution modifier and Proficiency Bonus). On a failed save, the creature has the {@condition Poisoned} condition until the start of your next turn.

entries.name: Snake Blood
entries: You have Advantage on saving throws to avoid or end the {@condition Poisoned} condition.

entries.name: Petrifying Gaze
entries: When you reach character level 5, you can take an Action to force a creature within 30 feet of you that you can see and that does not have the {@condition Blinded} condition to make a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 plus your Charisma modifier and Proficiency Bonus). On a failed save, the target has the {@condition Restrained} condition until the end of your next turn. While Restrained in this way, you can use Petrifying Gaze on that creature as a Bonus Action on subsequent turns. If it fails its saving throw three consecutive times, it has the {@condition Petrified} condition until the condition is ended by the {@spell Greater Restoration} spell or a similar effect.

They are despised and shunned by all other mortal species, and they must be careful to hide their identity when traveling in the civilized places of the world. Medusae have typically made bargains with some sort of fiend or fiendish power, but in some cases, they are oathbreakers who have displeased the gods or the Fates. Either way, they have been afflicted with the Curse of the Medusa as punishment, and recovery from the curse is not possible without the use of powerful magic--even {@spell Greater Restoration} is not enough to break the curse. Children born to medusae are also affected by the curse.

Truly, I have never considered myself to be cursed. I wished for gold, and gold I now have--in great quantities. Those who displease me are added to my lovely collection of statues. And I prefer the company of my snakes to that of lesser mortals.

race.name: Thylean Minotaur

sizeEntry.name: Size:
entries: Medium (6-8 feet tall, weighing 200-400 pounds).

Minotaurs are the descendants of an ancient tribe of humans who were cursed by the gods, transforming them into half-human, half-bull monstrosities. Although they are widely dismissed as unthinking brutes, they are in fact as diverse and as intelligent as any other species.

entries.name: Keen Snout
entries: You have a delicate nose. You gain proficiency in the Investigation skill and can detect strong odors from up to six miles away.

entries.name: Labyrinthine Vision
entries: You have Darkvision with a range of 60 feet and when you make an ability check to solve a maze or maze-like puzzle, you can use a total of 15 plus your Proficiency Bonus instead of rolling. Additionally, you automatically pass the saving throw for the {@spell Hypnotic Pattern} spell. Finally, you have Advantage on skill checks and saving throws against illusions that rely on sight.

entries.name: Colorblindness
entries: You see the world in shades of red and gray, leaving you incapable of discerning any color except for very bright reds.

entries.name: Cursed Transformation
entries: You can take a Bonus Action to cast the {@spell Polymorph} spell on yourself without expending a spell slot or requiring Concentration. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for it. You must choose the {@creature Bull|OotDLREHH} statblock. At character level 9, you can choose the {@creature Dire Bull|OotDLREHH} statblock as well, and starting at level 9, when you use this ability, you transform into a Dire Bull instead of a Bull.
You can use this trait a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus and regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

entries.name: Powerful Build
entries: You have Advantage on any ability check you make to end the {@condition Grappled} condition. You also count as one size larger when determining your carrying capacity.

Minotaurs possess uncommon strength, making them excellent warriors. The curse infuses their bodies with the power of a bull at all times, and their muscles seldom relax, even when they are drunk or asleep. In battle, minotaurs sometimes lose control of their emotions and fly into a rage. When this happens, the curse takes over, transforming them back into a full-fledged bull for a short period of time.

Minotaurs are widely shunned, because they are believed to be unthinking brutes who have been cursed by the gods. Most minotaurs gather together to form small farming or fishing communities, far from civilization.

entries.name: Minotaur Names
entries: Minotaurs generally prefer names that are short and simple. They typically punctuate their names with a snort or a sharp exhalation of air through their nostrils.
Names: Arxan, Braz, Dregxa, Elagore, Garnox, Horus, Kath, Luth, Manx, Parth, Raxus, Steth, Torag, Zark.

race.name: Thylean Satyr

sizeEntry.name: Size:
entries: Medium (4-5 feet tall, weighing 100-150 pounds).

Satyrs are a species of fey creatures with a strong link to the Feywild and all of the creatures and species that come from that place. They prefer forested wilderness but are not afraid to enter towns and cities to enjoy the company and other benefits of civilization.

entries.name: Fey Heritage
entries: You have Advantage on saving throws against being {@condition Charmed} or {@condition Frightened}, and spells can't put you to sleep.

entries.name: Memory for Music
entries: You have Expertise in the Performance skill.

entries.name: Enchanting Music
entries: You can cast the {@spell Minor Illusion} cantrip. When you reach level 3, you can cast the {@spell Sleep} spell once with this trait and regain the ability to do so when you finish a Long Rest. When you reach level 5, you can also cast the {@spell Suggestion} spell with this trait and regain the ability to do so when you finish a Long Rest. Casting these spells requires access to an instrument that you are proficient with. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for these spells (choose when you select this species). You can also cast these spells using any spell slots you have of the appropriate level.

Satyrs have the lower body of a goat and the upper body of an elf. A pair of goat-like horns sprout from their foreheads. Satyrs are in tune with their emotions to a degree that can be disturbing to other species. They want to experience everything: happiness, sadness, love, rage, etc. The only thing they avoid is boredom.

Satyrs don't have the same strained relationship with the civilized species of Thylea that the centaurs do. Satyrs can be found in many towns and villages throughout Thylea, as well as the great city of Mytros.

Trust these horn-headed fiends to get the better end of any deal you make with them. They'll ask to be paid in wine, and then drink you into poverty. I caught one of them tupping my sister behind the stables, and rather than having the good sense to be ashamed, he wrote a song about it. Sod them all, but the damned goats play music that could make the Muse herself weep.
entries.by: Delphion, Innkeeper of the Dragon's Tooth

entries.name: Satyr Names
entries: Male Names: Adrastos, Aeolus, Brontes, Castor, Cephalus, Glaucus, Helios, Iacchus, Kreios, Lycus, Melanthios, Okeanos, Proteus.
Female Names: Acantha, Astraea, Briseis, Clio, Erato, Harmonia, Ianthe, Jocasta, Melete, Phaedra, Phoebe, Selene, Tethys.

race.name: Thylean Siren

sizeEntry.name: Size:
entries: Medium (slightly shorter than humans, with a wingspan of about 6 feet).

Sirens are a species of winged, aquatic humanoids that typically dwell near rocky sea cliffs. They are famed for their beautiful voices, which they use to sing haunting lamentations, captivating listeners and transporting them to a bygone age.

entries.name: Enthralling Voice
entries: You have Advantage on Performance and Persuasion checks made with your voice. Additionally, your powerful lungs allow you to hold your breath for up to 1 hour.

entries.name: Wavering Emotions
entries: Whenever you finish a Short or Long Rest, choose one of the following options based on your feelings of joy or sadness:

items: Flight. Your joyful feelings grant you a Fly Speed of 30 feet. You can't use this speed if you are wearing Medium or Heavy armor.

Song of Sorrow. Your sorrowful feelings carry in a song with a powerful effect on anyone who hears it. You can cast each of the following spells once without expending a spell slot and regain the ability to do so again when you finish a Short or Long Rest, provided you are of the appropriate level: {@spell Charm Person} (character level 1), {@spell Enthrall} (character level 3), and {@spell Hold Person} (character level 5). When cast in this way, a creature with the {@condition Deafened} condition automatically passes its saving throw against the spell.

entries: Charisma is your spellcasting ability for these spells if you do not have the Spellcasting feature. If you do, you can use the same spellcasting ability as your Spellcasting feature instead.

Sirens have broad, feathered wings growing out of their backs, which allow them to fly like birds. For this reason, sirens are often employed as messengers. However, a siren can only fly when her heart is filled with light. Thus the saying, "A siren in good spirits may yet carry ill news."

Every siren is born with an abiding sense of sorrow that never fades--a soul-crushing grief caused by the loss of her ancestral home. From an early age, sirens learn to sing the ancient songs of their lost city, which evoke heart-wrenching memories of a time that will never come again.

entries.name: Siren Names
entries: Male Names: Alovar, Celeus, Everean, Gaiar, Helean, Inareus, Leiro, Meiar, Nerean, Oren, Reilan, Taeren.
Female Names: Alovarea, Celea, Everea, Gaia, Helena, Inarea, Leira, Meia, Nerea, Orena, Reilana, Taerena.

entries.name: Camouflage
entries: You gain Advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks when using the Hide Action in underground, rocky, or mountainous terrain.
Brown or black skinned, these are the predominant tallfolk and are the only tallfolk most raiders have ever encountered.

entries.name: Frostborn
entries: You have Resistance to Cold damage.

These tallfolk have a blue tinge to their skin and tend to be slightly larger than earth-children, hinting at a different ancestry. Other tallfolk are less welcoming of cold-children and they seldom hold any important position within the Risa.
